-tLORseEIzs.title: Walmart Video Repost: Copy Your Amazon Storefront Videos To Walmart Creator

paragraphs.heading: Your Amazon videos, on Walmart too
paragraphs.text: You already made videos for your Amazon storefront. Walmart Creator wants videos too. Making them twice is not happening. Video Repost copies them over for you.

paragraphs.heading: Power User feature
paragraphs.text: Quick note on plans. Video Repost, like everything in the Walmart Butler group, is a Power User feature. On the Beginner plan the group is hidden. Upgrade any time in Settings, under Subscription.

paragraphs.heading: Set it up: sign in to Walmart
paragraphs.text: Set it up walks you through signing in to Walmart Creator. Sign in once. If you are signed out later, the run stops and asks you to sign in again.

paragraphs.heading: Only exact matches
paragraphs.text: Here is the rule. It only reposts a video when the product is the exact same item on Walmart. Same barcode. Close is not good enough, so your video never lands on the wrong product.

paragraphs.heading: Review first, then automatic
paragraphs.text: Posting has two modes. Review matches before posting shows you the matches and waits for you. Post matches automatically posts them on its own. Start with Review.

paragraphs.heading: Max to post per run
paragraphs.text: Max to post per run is your speed limit. Walmart does not publish a limit, so start small, around 5 to 8 a day, until your account has some history.

paragraphs.heading: Skip out-of-stock products
paragraphs.text: Skip out-of-stock products does what it says. No point sending people to an item they cannot buy.

paragraphs.heading: Automatic schedule
paragraphs.text: The schedule runs it for you. Repeat every so many hours or days, and pick a first run time. Apply schedule turns it on.

paragraphs.heading: Video options
paragraphs.text: Video options are optional. Fit the video to Walmart's tall frame, trim it to 59 seconds, add a watermark, on-screen text or a QR code, or an AI voiceover.

paragraphs.heading: Exact Walmart matches
paragraphs.text: Down here are the matches. Each row is one of your storefront videos and the Walmart item it matched. In Review mode, this is the list you are approving.

paragraphs.heading: Filter by outcome
paragraphs.text: Show narrows the list to one outcome. Posted, failed, skipped, or not yet posted. Handy when you only want to see what went wrong.

paragraphs.heading: Post approved, Retry failed, Skip all
paragraphs.text: Post approved to Walmart sends the ones you approved. Retry failed tries the failed ones again. Skip all clears the list without posting anything.

paragraphs.heading: Needs Storefront Butler first
paragraphs.text: One thing it needs first. Storefront Butler. That is where your storefront videos come from. If it has never run, there is nothing to match, and this panel will tell you.

paragraphs.heading: Next step
paragraphs.text: Every post also shows up on the Walmart Butler hub. Your next step: run Storefront Butler, come back here, and press Start in Review mode.

0Db0me3aaS4.title: Group Invite Butler: Grow Your Facebook Group From a List of Emails

paragraphs.heading: The empty group
paragraphs.text: You made a Facebook group and it has four members. Meanwhile the Goldmines have collected hundreds of emails of creators in your niche. Group Invite Butler joins the two: it invites each address, one at a time, with a pause.

paragraphs.heading: Power User feature
paragraphs.text: Quick note on plans. Group Invite Butler is a Power User feature. On the Beginner plan it is hidden from the sidebar. Upgrade any time in Settings, under Subscription.

paragraphs.heading: One at a time matters
paragraphs.text: One at a time, with a pause, is the whole point. Facebook notices bursts, and a burst is how accounts get limited. Every invite is real, so nothing is pressed today.

paragraphs.heading: Which group
paragraphs.text: Facebook group URL is the group you manage and want people in. It is the one required field.

paragraphs.heading: Which account
paragraphs.text: Facebook account picks which signed-in account invites, or leave it on auto, whichever account posts to this group. Sign in to your accounts in Deals Butler first.

paragraphs.heading: Pacing
paragraphs.text: Pacing: seconds between invites, plus a random extra few seconds so the gaps are never identical. Forty-five seconds is the default and it is sensible.

paragraphs.heading: Sending limits
paragraphs.text: Sending limits: invites per day and invites per run. Your Facebook daily limit can stay at zero and the butler learns your account's real limit on its own.

paragraphs.heading: Newest first and retries
paragraphs.text: Invite newest emails first works the freshest addresses first. Automatically retry failed invites comes back to the ones that hit a temporary error.

paragraphs.heading: Fill the queue
paragraphs.text: The invite queue fills from the Instagram and Amazon Goldmines with Send to Group Invite Butler, or from a CSV with one email per row in the first column, or paste a handful.

paragraphs.heading: The queue
paragraphs.text: The queue: pending, sent and failed counts, and one row per email with where it came from and its status. Retry failed and Redo sent re-queue rows; Export CSV keeps a copy.

paragraphs.heading: Watch it run
paragraphs.text: Watch it run in the top bar keeps the browser on screen while it invites. It applies to every butler.

paragraphs.heading: Start
paragraphs.text: Start Group Invite Butler opens Chrome on that account, opens the group's invite form, and works through the queue at your pace.

paragraphs.heading: On a schedule
paragraphs.text: The schedule runs it on repeat, every hour or every day, using the limits above. Keep the app open and stay signed in.

paragraphs.heading: Next step
paragraphs.text: Your next step: paste your group URL, send a Goldmine harvest to the queue, cap it at twenty a day, and run it once while you watch.

0k7hSllci5w.title: Delete Posts and Comments: Bulk-Clean Your Facebook Deal Posts Safely

paragraphs.heading: Hundreds of dead posts
paragraphs.text: Post Amazon deals to Facebook for a year and you have hundreds of old posts with dead links. Cleaning them by hand is a weekend. Delete Posts and Comments does the sweep: you describe what should go, it finds every match, and removes them.

paragraphs.heading: Power User feature
paragraphs.text: Quick note on plans. Delete Posts & Comments is a Power User feature. On the Beginner plan it is hidden from the sidebar. Upgrade any time in Settings, under Subscription.

paragraphs.heading: Deleting is permanent
paragraphs.text: Facebook deletion is permanent. That is why the tool has a preview, a protect list, and a per-run cap, and why nothing is pressed in this video.

paragraphs.heading: Profile and scope
paragraphs.text: Facebook profile is the same list as Deals Butler. Where to clean up: My timeline is your own profile; Facebook groups or pages is where your deal posts went, so that is the usual pick.

paragraphs.heading: Groups and pages
paragraphs.text: The groups and pages come from Deals Butler's destinations. Tick the ones to clean, or paste more addresses one per line.

paragraphs.heading: Whose content
paragraphs.text: Whose content: my own content is the usual choice, Only posts Influencer Butler published is the surgical one, and the admin options reach other people's posts in groups you run.

paragraphs.heading: Posts, comments, deal content
paragraphs.text: Delete posts, comments, or both. Content type set to Deal content only keeps it to posts and comments with Amazon links, promo codes or paid-link tags. Any content is the wide net.

paragraphs.heading: Keywords
paragraphs.text: Only if it contains narrows it with words like deal drop or clearance. Never delete if it contains is the protect list, and it always wins.

paragraphs.heading: Age rules
paragraphs.text: Only older than so many days, and Always keep newer than, which protects recent posts. Skip pinned and featured posts stays on.

paragraphs.heading: The cap
paragraphs.text: Max deletions per run is your real safety net: an unattended run never deletes more than this. Delay between deletes and the extra random delay pace it like a person.

paragraphs.heading: Preview matches
paragraphs.text: Preview matches opens Chrome and scans without deleting anything. The results table then lists every match: type, content, where, and when.

paragraphs.heading: Read the results
paragraphs.text: Read that table before anything else. Matched, deleted, skipped and failed counts sit above it, and they add up across runs.

paragraphs.heading: Start cleanup
paragraphs.text: Start cleanup removes the matches, paced and capped. Watch it run in the top bar keeps the browser on screen. Put it on a schedule once you trust the filters; it always stays inside them and the cap.

paragraphs.heading: Next step
paragraphs.text: Your next step: groups or pages, deal content only, a protect list, a cap of twenty-five. Preview, read the table, then start.

1qZpD827EW0.title: Walmart Collection Builder: Rebuild Your Amazon Lists On Walmart

paragraphs.heading: Your Amazon lists, rebuilt on Walmart
paragraphs.text: You spent hours building your Amazon storefront lists. Walmart Creator wants collections too. Collection Builder rebuilds them for you.

paragraphs.heading: Power User feature
paragraphs.text: Quick note on plans. Collection Builder, like everything in the Walmart Butler group, is a Power User feature. On the Beginner plan the group is hidden. Upgrade any time in Settings, under Subscription.

paragraphs.heading: Start from your storefront
paragraphs.text: Paste your Amazon storefront link and press Find my lists. It reads every list you have made. Tick the ones you want and rebuild them all in one go.

paragraphs.heading: Or one list at a time
paragraphs.text: Or do one list at a time. Paste the Amazon list link here and press Import and match. The butler reads the products on it.

paragraphs.heading: Copy a Walmart collection
paragraphs.text: You can also start from a Walmart collection you already have, and build a fresh one from it.

paragraphs.heading: Matching
paragraphs.text: Matching decides how strict to be. Exact matches only, or allow similar items when the exact one is not on Walmart.

paragraphs.heading: Use OpenAI
paragraphs.text: Use OpenAI lets the AI write the collection name and description, and pick the closest Walmart products. Without a key it uses a plain fallback, and the panel tells you.

paragraphs.heading: Name and description
paragraphs.text: Name and description. Keep the Amazon ones, or let the butler write new ones that fit Walmart.

paragraphs.heading: Review every pick
paragraphs.text: Nothing is created until you review it. Every pick shows the Amazon product next to its Walmart match. Untick anything that is off, then press Create collection.

paragraphs.heading: Your collections
paragraphs.text: Collections you have built live here. Each one links to the live collection on your Walmart storefront.

paragraphs.heading: Share it
paragraphs.text: From here, share a collection on Facebook, add it to your Deals queue, or add it to your Foyer page. Remove out-of-stock items cleans up an older collection.

paragraphs.heading: Needs a Walmart sign-in
paragraphs.text: It needs your Walmart Creator sign-in, which you do once with the sign-in button. And an OpenAI key in API Integrations if you want the AI picks.

paragraphs.heading: Next step
paragraphs.text: Your next step: paste one Amazon list link, press Import and match, and review the picks.

3gWuJHgGeds.title: Retag Butler: Fix Out-of-Stock Products in Your Amazon Posts

paragraphs.heading: Money quietly leaking
paragraphs.text: Products go out of stock. Your old posts keep getting views, and every one of those views now earns nothing. Retag Butler finds those dead links and adds a product people can actually buy.

paragraphs.heading: Power User feature
paragraphs.text: Quick note on plans. Retag Butler is a Power User feature. On the Beginner plan it is hidden from the sidebar. Upgrade any time in Settings, under Subscription.

paragraphs.heading: It adds, never removes
paragraphs.text: The reassuring part: it never removes your old tag. It adds the replacement alongside, so your history stays intact and the link points at something live.

paragraphs.heading: What it needs
paragraphs.text: It reads which products are unavailable from Storefront Butler, so sync that first. Your storefront URL comes from Settings, and the status line here confirms it is set and signed in.

paragraphs.heading: Your numbers
paragraphs.text: The overview: pieces scanned, stale products, untagged pieces, replacement candidates matched, and new products tagged.

paragraphs.heading: After matching
paragraphs.text: The control that matters most. Manual review, then retag approved puts every suggestion in a list and waits for you. Start here. Auto-approve tags matches above the threshold on its own.

paragraphs.heading: The auto-tag threshold
paragraphs.text: Auto-tag threshold is the confidence line for auto mode, seventy out of a hundred by default. Keep it at seventy or above unless you review results.

paragraphs.heading: Min title similarity
paragraphs.text: Min title similarity decides which candidates appear in the list at all. Lower it to see more, including weak ones you can reject.

paragraphs.heading: Pick from a list or single best
paragraphs.text: When a match is found, pick from a short list or take the single best. Amazon Visual Match uses Amazon's own image matching: more accurate, and slower.

paragraphs.heading: Run
paragraphs.text: Run scans your storefront, finds the stale products, and matches replacements. Watch it run in the top bar keeps the browser on screen.

paragraphs.heading: The queue
paragraphs.text: Then the queue, as cards or a table. Each one shows the content, the stale product, the candidate, and its score, with Approve, Skip and Re-match. Filter by status, type or reason.

paragraphs.heading: Approve, then retag
paragraphs.text: Approve selected marks the ones you agree with, and Run retags on approved writes only those to Amazon. Export diff CSV keeps a before-and-after record.

paragraphs.heading: On a schedule
paragraphs.text: Schedule recurring runs keeps it going, every few days, so new dead links get caught early.

paragraphs.heading: Next step
paragraphs.text: Your next step: sync Storefront Butler, keep Manual review, press Run, and approve your first ten swaps. Then decide whether auto mode earns your trust.

3q62ifVu-io.title: Campaign Deals: See Which of Your Campaign Products Are On Sale

paragraphs.heading: Post it while it is cheap
paragraphs.text: A product on sale sells far better. Campaign Deals tells you which products in your campaigns are discounted right now, so you post them while the price is low.

paragraphs.heading: Power User feature
paragraphs.text: Quick note on plans. Campaign Deals is a Power User feature. On the Beginner plan it is hidden from the sidebar. Upgrade any time in Settings, under Subscription.

paragraphs.heading: Where the list comes from
paragraphs.text: It does not go hunting. It reuses the price data CC Check already collects through the Creators API, so if this screen is empty, run CC Check first.

paragraphs.heading: Two numbers
paragraphs.text: Up top: how many products are on sale now, and how many products are in your campaigns in total. Last refreshed tells you how fresh the prices are.

paragraphs.heading: Include available
paragraphs.text: Include available adds on-sale products from campaigns you could join but have not yet. A quick way to spot a discount worth accepting a campaign for.

paragraphs.heading: Refresh Deals
paragraphs.text: Refresh Deals asks Amazon for today's prices. It only reads, no browser opens, and nothing is accepted. Press it and the numbers move.

paragraphs.heading: Three sources in one table
paragraphs.text: The tabs split the sources: Creator Connections campaigns, EPC deals, which are Earn on Clicks offers with a forecast per click, and Promo codes.

paragraphs.heading: The table
paragraphs.text: Each row: the product, percent off, sale price, what it was, when the deal ends, your commission, the EPC, and a promo code if there is one. Deal ends is the column to respect.

paragraphs.heading: Filters
paragraphs.text: Filters narrow it: minimum percent off, minimum commission, minimum EPC, a max price, or only products with a promo or coupon. Sort by percent off puts the biggest discount first.

paragraphs.heading: Search
paragraphs.text: Or search by brand or product code when you know what you are after.

paragraphs.heading: Social bonus and AI Post
paragraphs.text: Tick Social bonus on a row to remember a brand that pays extra for a social post. AI Post in the Actions column drafts a post for that product right away.

paragraphs.heading: Refresh on a timer
paragraphs.text: Set a start time and how often to repeat, then Enable Schedule, and the prices refresh on their own.

paragraphs.heading: Next step
paragraphs.text: Your next step: once a week, press Refresh Deals, sort by percent off, and post whatever is cheapest with a deal still running.

3XDo7C1iGGw.title: Message Brands: Automate Your Amazon Creator Connections Outreach

paragraphs.heading: The problem
paragraphs.text: You know which brands your videos sell for. Turning that into a campaign means opening Creator Connections and typing the same pitch, brand after brand, until you give up. Message Brands types it for you.

paragraphs.heading: Included in the Beginner plan
paragraphs.text: Quick note on plans. Message Brands is included in the Beginner plan, so everyone has it.

paragraphs.heading: Filters decide who gets contacted
paragraphs.text: Before anything else, Keywords and Filters, the child workspace right under Message Brands. It decides who gets contacted. Leave it empty and nothing narrows the run.

paragraphs.heading: Add a keyword to target
paragraphs.text: Add the keywords or brand names you want to go after. Every campaign that matches one becomes a target.

paragraphs.heading: And what to leave alone
paragraphs.text: Two skip lists sit under it: words you never want in a campaign title, and brands to leave alone entirely. A skip always wins.

paragraphs.heading: Back to Message Brands
paragraphs.text: With filters set, back to Message Brands. Everything from here is what the message says and how fast it goes out.

paragraphs.heading: Write your message
paragraphs.text: Write the default message once. Use brandName and campaignName in curly braces and each brand gets its own name filled in, so it never reads like a blast. Your storefront URL, address and media kit are placeholders too.

paragraphs.heading: Never message twice
paragraphs.text: Skip brands you have already messaged stays on. It skips any brand with a message or a conversation already, whether the butler sent it or you did.

paragraphs.heading: Set your pace
paragraphs.text: Daily message cap and pause between sends are your pacing. Start small so you can read what landed in your Creator Connections inbox before you open it up.

paragraphs.heading: Campaign value filters
paragraphs.text: Campaign value filters are where this gets good. Turn them on and a brand only gets messaged if its campaign clears your bars for product price, estimated monthly revenue, and commission.

paragraphs.heading: Skip the products nobody buys
paragraphs.text: Minimum product reviews and Only if the product has a Best Sellers Rank keep you out of a closet of samples for products that do not sell. Both read the Creators API, so connect it in Settings first.

paragraphs.heading: Only products your audience can buy
paragraphs.text: The country availability filter checks each campaign's products against the Amazon store your audience buys from, and skips brands with nothing buyable there.

paragraphs.heading: Follow-ups
paragraphs.text: Most brands do not answer the first message. Enable follow-ups, pick six, twelve or twenty-four hours, and write a shorter nudge. Variants rotate the wording.

paragraphs.heading: Templates
paragraphs.text: New template saves a message per keyword or brand, so a kitchen brand gets a kitchen pitch and the default only covers the rest.

paragraphs.heading: Now press Run
paragraphs.text: That is everything configured. Run opens Chrome in your signed-in Amazon session, works through the campaigns your filters matched, and posts your message on each brand's Creator Connections page.

paragraphs.heading: Watch it work
paragraphs.text: Watch the run status fill in: current brand, the search term that surfaced it, how many sent, and the reason for anything it skipped. Watch it run in the top bar keeps the browser on screen.

paragraphs.heading: Follow it into Messenger
paragraphs.text: Now the part that pays off later. Every message shows up in Messenger Butler tagged with the keyword it went out under. Run its initial harvest once so it reads your conversations.

paragraphs.heading: Which keywords earn replies
paragraphs.text: Search by brand or keyword, and you see exactly which search terms produced replies, so you can stop spending sends on the ones that never do.

paragraphs.heading: Next step
paragraphs.text: Your next step: one keyword, a message you would be happy to receive, a daily cap of ten. Run it, and come back to Messenger Butler in a few days to read what replied.

54wdnHuUZY8.title: Find Your Instagram Channel ID To Post Deals or Collages With Your Influencer Butler

paragraphs.heading: Find the channel link
paragraphs.text: First things first, we are going to have to find the Instagram channel link. Go to your Instagram account and click on the channel that you want to be posting in. Then click on the share icon and copy the link. Send it to yourself in an email.

paragraphs.heading: Open the browser console
paragraphs.text: Open the link on your computer, then right-click and select Inspect in the menu. Then go to the Console tab, which you can find here, and click it.

paragraphs.heading: Paste the formula
paragraphs.text: Copy and paste the formula provided. Sometimes there may be text in the console already; you can clear that out first by selecting the clear button. The browser may also tell you to type allow pasting before it lets you paste. Type that in, press Enter, and paste the formula again. This prints the channel ID, which is what we want.

paragraphs.heading: Verify the channel
paragraphs.text: Then go over and verify that it is the right channel you are looking for, in the account you are logged in with that can message in the channel. Here is the finished link.

paragraphs.heading: Add it to Influencer Butler
paragraphs.text: Take that link, copy it, go to Influencer Butler, open Amazon Deals Butler, then Social Destinations, and paste the link in there. Then you are good to go and you can start sharing your deals to your Instagram channel.

5vq30g1NIEE.title: Levanta Message Brands: Automate Your Pitches on the Levanta Brand Network

paragraphs.heading: Another network, same chore
paragraphs.text: Levanta connects creators with brands that pay for influencer marketing. Pitching each approved brand by hand is the same chore as Creator Connections. Levanta Message Brands does the pitching, the same way Amazon Message Brands does.

paragraphs.heading: Power User feature
paragraphs.text: Quick note on plans. Levanta Message Brands is a Power User feature. On the Beginner plan it is hidden from the sidebar. Upgrade any time in Settings, under Subscription.

paragraphs.heading: What it needs
paragraphs.text: An approved Levanta account, a signed-in Levanta session in Chrome, and your Levanta API key in Settings. Email Extractor runs alongside and collects each brand's contact email.

paragraphs.heading: Run status
paragraphs.text: Run status: usage, sent, the current brand, and the search term that surfaced it, filling in while a run goes.

paragraphs.heading: The default message
paragraphs.text: The default message is sent when no template matches. Use brandName and campaignName in braces, and address and media kit if the brief asks for them. Keep it short and personable.

paragraphs.heading: Follow-ups
paragraphs.text: Enable follow-ups sends a second message after six, twelve or twenty-four hours, with daysSinceMessage available for the wording.

paragraphs.heading: Keywords or brand name
paragraphs.text: Keyword and brand filters decide who is contacted. Add the keywords or brands to target; leave it empty and every approved brand qualifies.

paragraphs.heading: Skip lists
paragraphs.text: Skip keywords in campaign title and brands to skip take campaigns and brands out entirely. A skip always wins.

paragraphs.heading: Never twice, and a cap
paragraphs.text: Exclude brands with messages already sent keeps it from pitching anyone twice. Daily message cap stops the run at that many sends. Start small.

paragraphs.heading: Templates
paragraphs.text: Keyword and brand templates send a different pitch when a keyword or brand matches: name it, list the matchers, and add a few variations.

paragraphs.heading: Run Levanta Now
paragraphs.text: Run Levanta Now opens Chrome on your Levanta session and works through the matching brands. Watch it run in the top bar keeps it on screen. Not pressed today.

paragraphs.heading: Next step
paragraphs.text: Your next step: connect Levanta in Settings, write the default message, add one keyword, cap it at five, and run it once while you watch.

83CohIIKP_c.title: Shopping Butler: Find The Best Product To Buy Or Feature

paragraphs.heading: Which one should you buy, or feature?
paragraphs.text: You need a laptop stand. Which one is the best buy? And which one would earn you the most if you featured it? Shopping Butler answers both in one search.

paragraphs.heading: Included in the Beginner plan
paragraphs.text: A quick note on plans. Shopping Butler is free, and it is included in the Beginner plan. Everyone has it. It is a shopper's tool, not a poster, so there is nothing to run or schedule.

paragraphs.heading: Where to shop
paragraphs.text: Where to shop sits above the search box. Tick Amazon, Walmart, or both. Both are on by default, and your choices are saved for next time.

paragraphs.heading: Countries
paragraphs.text: Countries picks which Amazon sites to search. US is on by default. Other countries use your own Amazon keys from AI and Data Keys, so they stay greyed out until you connect them. Walmart is US only.

paragraphs.heading: Type what you are shopping for
paragraphs.text: Type what you are shopping for, in plain words.

paragraphs.heading: Search
paragraphs.text: Press Search. It searches Amazon and Walmart at the same time and scores every product it finds.

paragraphs.heading: Searching both stores
paragraphs.text: This takes a moment, because it is reading real product pages. Each result gets four scores: price, product quality from its rating and reviews, the commission you would earn, and how crowded it already is.

paragraphs.heading: Rank for: buy, balanced, or feature
paragraphs.text: Rank for switches the order. Best to buy puts cheap and good first. Best to feature puts the most commission and the least crowded first. Balanced is a bit of both.

paragraphs.heading: The results
paragraphs.text: Here are the results. Each card shows the price, the rating, what you would earn, and how many creator videos already cover it. A great product nobody has covered yet is your best opening.

paragraphs.heading: Check saturation
paragraphs.text: Check saturation looks up the real number of creator videos on each product's Amazon page. It is optional, and it takes a little longer.

paragraphs.heading: Cards or table
paragraphs.text: Switch to Table when you want to compare the numbers side by side.

paragraphs.heading: Next step
paragraphs.text: Found a winner? Buy it for your next review video, or feature it as a deal. Your next step: type what you are shopping for and press Search.

8ESZ60YY8h0.title: Content Butler: Plan What to Film Next on a Calendar

paragraphs.heading: A backlog with no dates
paragraphs.text: You have a backlog of products you mean to film and no system for when. Content Butler is the calendar: each entry is a product parked on a day, and the sidebar holds everything you have not scheduled yet.

paragraphs.heading: Power User feature
paragraphs.text: Quick note on plans. Content Butler is a Power User feature. On the Beginner plan it is hidden from the sidebar. Upgrade any time in Settings, under Subscription.

paragraphs.heading: Three views
paragraphs.text: Monthly for the shape of the month, Weekly for what you are shooting this week, Daily for a busy shoot day, and List for a flat searchable list.

paragraphs.heading: Back to the month
paragraphs.text: Back to the month. Each day holds a few entries, and overdue ones are marked. The Overdue button filters to them.

paragraphs.heading: Tags
paragraphs.text: Tags track each entry's stage: ideation, ready to film, filming, editing, awaiting approval, ready to publish. Filter by tag or add your own.

paragraphs.heading: Unassigned products
paragraphs.text: Unassigned products is the sidebar: what Orders Butler found you still need a photo, a vertical or a horizontal video for. Drag a card onto a day to schedule it, or drop it back to unschedule.

paragraphs.heading: Quick add
paragraphs.text: Quick add a product adds one that did not come from your orders: a title, an optional ASIN, and shooting notes.

paragraphs.heading: Income report
paragraphs.text: The income report, like Collab Butler's, lists the products brands sent you with their value, for tax time.

paragraphs.heading: Export
paragraphs.text: Export CSV takes the plan to a spreadsheet. Delete All clears the calendar, so leave it alone.

paragraphs.heading: Next step
paragraphs.text: Your next step: drag five products from Unassigned onto next week, and tag them ready to film.

8pw7XHXgOvM.title: Facebook Message Butler: Message Group Members One at a Time, Paced and Unique

paragraphs.heading: The same message, a hundred times
paragraphs.text: You want to message the members of a group. Sending them all the same words, fast, is how accounts get flagged. Facebook Message Butler writes one message with choices built in, so every person gets a slightly different version, and sends them slowly.

paragraphs.heading: Power User feature
paragraphs.text: Quick note on plans. Facebook Message Butler is a Power User feature. On the Beginner plan it is hidden from the sidebar. Upgrade any time in Settings, under Subscription.

paragraphs.heading: Which account
paragraphs.text: Send from picks the Facebook account, the same logins as Deals Butler. Sign in opens a real Facebook window if you need to, and Verify sign-in confirms it with a green badge.

paragraphs.heading: Who to message
paragraphs.text: Who to message: the members of a group you belong to, the followers of a Page, or a list you paste or load from a CSV. Paste the group address, decide whether admins are included, and press Find recipients to fill the queue. Anyone you already messaged is skipped.

paragraphs.heading: Your message
paragraphs.text: Your message, written once. Put choices in braces, like Hi, Hey, Hello, and it picks one per person. Use firstName for their name. The counter shows how many unique variations that makes.

paragraphs.heading: The toolbar
paragraphs.text: The toolbar adds options to a selected word, inserts a greeting or a sign-off, or drops in their name.

paragraphs.heading: Preview variations
paragraphs.text: Preview variations shows a few sample messages so you can read how they land before anything goes out.

paragraphs.heading: Individual messages
paragraphs.text: How to send: individual messages, one private message per person, is the safe choice. Group chat adds several people into one thread and Facebook limits it heavily.

paragraphs.heading: Pacing formulas
paragraphs.text: Pacing and limits: pick a ready-made formula, Cautious for a new account, Conservative as the default, or set your own seconds between messages and messages per hour and per day. Ease in gently and Pause overnight keep it looking human.

paragraphs.heading: Watch it run
paragraphs.text: Watch it run in the top bar keeps the browser on screen so you can watch the first few go out. It applies to every butler.

paragraphs.heading: Start
paragraphs.text: Start Facebook Message Butler opens Chrome on that account and works through the queue at your pace. Every message is real, so nothing is pressed today.

paragraphs.heading: Replies
paragraphs.text: Check for replies reads the conversations it started and marks who answered, on demand or on its own schedule.

paragraphs.heading: Next step
paragraphs.text: Your next step: one group, the Conservative formula, a message with three greeting choices. Preview it, then send ten while you watch.

9FEiqUFkMDM.title: Earnings Intelligence: See Which Amazon Products Actually Earned

paragraphs.heading: Read-only
paragraphs.text: It is read-only. It never opens a browser and never changes anything on Amazon. It reads what Daily Commission Butler, Storefront Butler, Orders Butler and CC Check already collected.

paragraphs.heading: Filters
paragraphs.text: Pick a date range, a source type, a marketplace or a storefront, and the whole page follows.

paragraphs.heading: Summary
paragraphs.text: The summary line: total commission, units, and how many ASINs earned in that window.

paragraphs.heading: ASIN Explorer
paragraphs.text: ASIN Explorer is the detail. One row per earning product: commission, units, active days, last seen, and where it sold.

paragraphs.heading: Six views
paragraphs.text: Across the top, six views of the same data: ASIN Explorer, Top Performers, Recovered Winners, Harvest Funnel, Monthly Breakdown, and Conversion Leak, which lists posted deals that went dead and what they cost you.

paragraphs.heading: Monthly breakdown
paragraphs.text: Monthly Breakdown splits your commissions by month across every revenue source. Export it to CSV or Excel, or sync it to the web dashboard.

paragraphs.heading: Next step
paragraphs.text: Your next step: open Top Performers and feature your top three again.

aV7uG4D4-PM.title: Action Queue: See Every Scheduled Task Across Your Butlers

paragraphs.heading: Power User feature
paragraphs.text: Quick note on plans. Action Queue is a Power User feature. On the Beginner plan it is hidden from the sidebar. Upgrade any time in Settings, under Subscription.

paragraphs.heading: Nothing to set up
paragraphs.text: There is nothing to set up. Other butlers put tasks here when you schedule them: searches, catalog refreshes, campaign syncs, posting rounds.

paragraphs.heading: Filter by workspace
paragraphs.text: Filter by workspace to see one butler's schedule, and search actions by name.

paragraphs.heading: The counts
paragraphs.text: Overdue, next hour, and today, so you know at a glance whether anything slipped.

paragraphs.heading: Pending
paragraphs.text: Pending lists each task with its time, how far away it is, and which schedule it belongs to. The small x removes one task; the next schedule pass puts it back if the schedule is still on.

paragraphs.heading: Completed
paragraphs.text: Completed is the record of what already ran.

paragraphs.heading: Next step
paragraphs.text: Your next step: open it before bed and read what is set to run overnight.

bf6bqNhJxjg.title: Instagram Close Friends Butler: Auto-Add New Followers to Close Friends Safely

paragraphs.text: Close Friends Stories are where the exclusive offers and the high-converting content live. Adding every new follower by hand is scroll and tap, one at a time. Close Friends Butler does the adding, with the brakes on.

paragraphs.heading: Power User feature
paragraphs.text: Quick note on plans. Instagram Close Friends Butler is a Power User feature. On the Beginner plan it is hidden from the sidebar. Upgrade any time in Settings, under Subscription.

paragraphs.heading: A real change
paragraphs.text: It adds real people to your real list from your signed-in Instagram session. Everyone added can see your Close Friends Stories from that moment, so nothing is pressed today.

paragraphs.heading: Your numbers
paragraphs.text: Friends added, added today, failed or skipped, and unique creators.

paragraphs.heading: Max per run
paragraphs.text: Run settings are the brakes. Max per run stops this run after that many adds. Twenty-five is the default.

paragraphs.heading: Per hour and per day
paragraphs.text: Per hour and per day are rolling ceilings. Twenty an hour and two hundred a day are the defaults, and Instagram action-blocks accounts that push past its invisible limit, so do not raise them much.

paragraphs.heading: Lifetime total
paragraphs.text: Lifetime total is a brake for long-running schedules: the butler stops at the lowest active cap.

paragraphs.heading: Delays
paragraphs.text: Min and max delay put a random pause between adds, seven to fifteen seconds, which looks more human than a fixed gap.

paragraphs.heading: Auto-harvest followers
paragraphs.text: Auto-harvest followers scans your newest followers each run. That is where the adds come from.

paragraphs.heading: Queue and exclusions
paragraphs.text: Add a handle manually and it is processed first. Skip usernames leaves people out of the next run only. The do-not-add list is forever: brands, family, anyone who should never be on the inside.

paragraphs.heading: Run days
paragraphs.text: Run days picks the weekdays the schedule may fire. Manual runs work any day.

paragraphs.heading: Run
paragraphs.text: Run opens Chrome on your Instagram session and starts adding. Watch it run in the top bar keeps the browser on screen. Stop ends it.

paragraphs.heading: History
paragraphs.text: Results list every add with its date, username and status. Export CSV keeps a copy.

paragraphs.heading: Next step
paragraphs.text: Your next step: keep the default caps, add two names to the do-not-add list, and run it once while you watch.

C_vtu1BFjow.title: Collab Butler: Track Every Brand Collaboration on One Board

paragraphs.text: Once you work with brands at any scale, you need somewhere to track each deal that is not your inbox. Collab Butler is a board: one card per collaboration, moving through stages as it progresses.

paragraphs.heading: Power User feature
paragraphs.text: Quick note on plans. Collab Butler is a Power User feature. On the Beginner plan it is hidden from the sidebar. Upgrade any time in Settings, under Subscription.

paragraphs.heading: Your numbers
paragraphs.text: Active collabs, due soon, overdue, and a count per tag: free sample, form, awaiting approval, shipped, published.

paragraphs.heading: Insights
paragraphs.text: Insights opens pipeline value, completed this month, the overdue rate, your top brands and a brand directory.

paragraphs.heading: Income report
paragraphs.text: Income report lists the products brands sent you, with their value and any cash payout, for tax time. Pick a date range and export it.

paragraphs.heading: Search, filter, sort
paragraphs.text: Search collabs, filter by stage or tag, and sort by recently updated, brand, keyword, due date or your own order.

paragraphs.heading: Board or list
paragraphs.text: Board shows the stages as columns, negotiating, shipped, in progress, submitted, published. List is the same cards as rows.

paragraphs.heading: Tags
paragraphs.text: Drag a workflow tag onto a card: awaiting approval, editing, ready to film, ready to publish, needs brief. Add Tag makes your own.

paragraphs.heading: Reminders
paragraphs.text: Enable reminders surfaces due-soon and overdue cards with one-click actions.

paragraphs.heading: New Collab
paragraphs.text: New Collab adds a card: brand, stage, deadline, payout, notes. Pitch Butler tracks the deal before it closes; this board picks up after.

paragraphs.heading: Import and export
paragraphs.text: Import brings collabs in from a CSV in the sample layout; Export JSON and CSV take them out. Delete All is literal and permanent, so export first.

paragraphs.heading: Next step
paragraphs.text: Your next step: add your three live deals as cards, tag what is awaiting approval, and turn on reminders.

d5nzVFOI2lc.title: Instagram Goldmine: Discover the Brands Paying Creators in Your Niche

paragraphs.heading: Who is paying?
paragraphs.text: The easiest brands to pitch are the ones already paying creators like you. Instagram Goldmine finds them: it starts from a few creators in your niche, follows Instagram's suggested-for-you trail, and collects every post tagged as paid.

paragraphs.heading: Power User feature
paragraphs.text: Quick note on plans. Instagram Goldmine is a Power User feature. On the Beginner plan it is hidden from the sidebar. Upgrade any time in Settings, under Subscription.

paragraphs.heading: It only looks
paragraphs.text: It reads public profiles and posts. No follows, no likes, no messages. Sign in to Instagram once here and every Instagram butler shares that session.

paragraphs.heading: Seeds
paragraphs.text: Seed usernames: three to ten creators whose audience overlaps yours. Handles or profile links both work.

paragraphs.heading: Run mode and size
paragraphs.text: Run mode decides how wide it goes, min followers sets the floor, and max suggested per seed and max profiles per run cap the walk. Keep the first run small.

paragraphs.heading: What counts as paid
paragraphs.text: What counts as paid: posts with hashtag ad disclosures, posts with the paid partnership label, or posts with tagged or mentioned brands. Tick the ones that matter to you.

paragraphs.heading: Safe mode
paragraphs.text: Safe mode doubles the human delays. Slower, and far less likely to get the session blocked. Leave it on.

paragraphs.heading: Harvest emails
paragraphs.text: Harvest tagged brand emails pulls the contact email from each brand it finds, and Also check the bio-link website chases the email one step further. Slower, but that is the pitch list.

paragraphs.heading: Watch it run
paragraphs.text: Watch it run in the top bar keeps the browser on screen. It applies to every butler.

paragraphs.heading: Start Discovery
paragraphs.text: Start Discovery opens Chrome and walks the graph. It takes a while, so start it and come back. Not pressed today.

paragraphs.heading: Qualifying posts
paragraphs.text: The qualifying posts table: the creator, their followers and engagement rate, the post, why it qualified, the brands mentioned, and the brand email when it found one. Search it, or filter by pitched status.

paragraphs.heading: Send it on
paragraphs.text: Tick rows and Send to Pitch Butler carries the brand, the creator and the post across, or send the creators to Group Invite Butler. Export CSV keeps the lot.

paragraphs.heading: Next step
paragraphs.text: Your next step: three seeds, twenty-five profiles, safe mode on, harvest emails on. Run it once, then pitch the brands that show up twice.

DnNapPVfNKg.title: Publish Benable Lists From One Keyword: List Publishing

paragraphs.heading: One keyword, a finished list
paragraphs.text: You want a Benable list full of good products, ready to share. List Publishing builds it from one keyword and publishes it to your Benable account.

paragraphs.heading: Sign in to Benable first
paragraphs.text: First, sign in. Click Sign in to Benable and a browser window opens to log in. Other Benable butlers share that login.

paragraphs.heading: Publish needs your OpenAI key
paragraphs.text: Publish stays switched off until your OpenAI key is connected, in AI and Data Keys. If it is missing, a notice near the top points you there.

paragraphs.heading: Amazon products need the Creators API
paragraphs.text: When products come from Amazon, search uses your Amazon Creators API connection. Set it up in Amazon Butler, then Settings.

paragraphs.heading: Watch it run, in the top bar
paragraphs.text: In the top bar, Watch it run shows or hides the browser windows automations use. It starts off on a new install.

paragraphs.heading: Type your niche
paragraphs.text: Now the main input. Type a niche keyword, like kitchen gadgets or dog deals. Broad works, and specific works too.

paragraphs.heading: List by: keyword or brand
paragraphs.text: List by can switch to Brand name. Then every list showcases one brand's products.

paragraphs.heading: Pick your marketplace
paragraphs.text: Marketplace is where the products come from. Match it to your affiliate account, so the links earn commission.

paragraphs.heading: Four list sources
paragraphs.text: List source has four choices. Marketplace uses that store. Retailers only uses Target, Walmart, and the App Store. Curated skips affiliate links. Non-product lists things not for sale.

paragraphs.heading: Keep the first run small
paragraphs.text: Number of lists starts at 4 to 4. Use the same number in both boxes for an exact count. For a first run, try 1 to 1. Sections per list starts at 3 to 6.

paragraphs.heading: Affiliate disclosure
paragraphs.text: Affiliate disclosure is the wording Butler adds, and it uses (AD) when blank. Pick the title, description, or notes. Only the description is ticked to start.

paragraphs.heading: Open Advanced settings
paragraphs.text: More publishing options live in Advanced settings. Open it before your first real run.

paragraphs.heading: Only products with a campaign
paragraphs.text: Only publish products with a campaign starts ticked. It keeps Amazon products in Creator Connections or with an SPCC offer. A list left with too few of them can be held instead of published, and the Latest run card says why.

paragraphs.heading: Make lists public
paragraphs.text: Make lists public after create starts ticked. New Benable lists start hidden, and this makes them public. Untick it to review a list first.

paragraphs.heading: Notes and covers
paragraphs.text: Skip per-product notes is for quick test runs, since notes help a list rank. Generate list covers is on to start.

paragraphs.heading: Share your lists
paragraphs.text: Under Share your lists, Share new lists automatically is off to start. Turn it on and tick where to share, like Pinterest or Telegram. These use the Social Destinations you set up in Amazon Deals Butler.

paragraphs.heading: List size
paragraphs.text: Hold lists too short to rank starts ticked. Butler tops up short lists toward your target. It treats 16 products as the minimum to rank, aims for 21, and trims to 25.

paragraphs.heading: Retailer mix
paragraphs.text: Retailer mix can add a few non-Amazon items, like App Store apps, Target products, or your own links. All start off. With the campaign filter ticked, as it is to start, those extras are dropped, so untick it to keep them.

paragraphs.heading: Get list ideas
paragraphs.text: The AI list-idea generator suggests list titles for a niche. It publishes nothing. List Idea Packs offer ready-made ideas by season or holiday.

paragraphs.heading: The List Ideas queue
paragraphs.text: Ideas wait in the List Ideas queue. Type a title and press Add, or paste many niches, one per line.

paragraphs.heading: Default output
paragraphs.text: Default output sets whether an idea builds one list or a full collection. Publish all queued runs every idea that is not done yet.

paragraphs.heading: Auto-run
paragraphs.text: Auto-run works on a schedule. It is off until you switch it on. Choose every 1, 3, 6, 12, or 24 hours.

paragraphs.heading: Custom schedule and active hours
paragraphs.text: Custom adds a time of day, certain days only, and a random delay. Only run during active hours is off to start. Once ticked, it skips runs outside your hours, which are set to 9 AM to 9 PM to start.

paragraphs.heading: Lists per day
paragraphs.text: Lists per day runs that many times a day, publishing one idea from your queue each time. The runs spread across your active hours if you turned those on, or across the whole day if not. Leave it at 0 to use the schedule.

paragraphs.heading: What each run does
paragraphs.text: On each fire sets the job. Choices include refreshing saved lists, publishing the current niche as a fresh collection, or publishing one new list from the queue. Refresh needs list addresses below.

paragraphs.heading: Fix SPCC links
paragraphs.text: Fix SPCC links swaps in your accepted SPCC link on lists you already published. Check links is a dry run. Fix links asks you to confirm.

paragraphs.heading: Organize into collections
paragraphs.text: Scan my profile suggests which lists belong together in a collection. Untick any you do not want. Applying asks you to confirm.

paragraphs.heading: Watch the status pill
paragraphs.text: Once you click Publish, this pill names each step, like Finding products for your niche. Stop switches on only during a run.

paragraphs.heading: Read the Latest run card
paragraphs.text: When a run ends, a Latest run card appears under this bar, with the collection, a predicted optimization score from 0 to 100 per list, and a link to each list.

paragraphs.heading: If lists are held
paragraphs.text: If lists were held, the card says why. Publish them anyway turns off the filter that held them, and runs again.

paragraphs.heading: Run totals and past runs
paragraphs.text: Run totals add up lists and products. Past runs shows your recent runs, with a Resume button when one can continue.

paragraphs.heading: Next: Published Products
paragraphs.text: Then open Published Products to see every product you published and why it was picked, and List Optimize to audit a list and get fixes.

paragraphs.heading: Your first run
paragraphs.text: So a first run goes: sign in, connect OpenAI and the Amazon Creators API, type a niche, set lists to 1 to 1, and click Publish. Then read the Latest run card.

DsWkQUGHxyA.title: Campaign Alert Butler: Be First When a Brand Posts a Creator Connections Campaign

paragraphs.text: The best campaigns fill fast. By the time you check, the brand you love has posted one and it is full. Campaign Alert Butler watches your brands and tells you the moment they post something new.

paragraphs.heading: Included in the Beginner plan
paragraphs.text: Quick note on plans. Campaign Alert Butler is included in the Beginner plan, so everyone has it.

paragraphs.heading: Your numbers
paragraphs.text: Brands followed, how many campaigns those brands have live right now, and how many alerts are waiting for you.

paragraphs.heading: Follow a brand
paragraphs.text: Type a brand name and the matches show how many campaigns it is running and its best rate. Press Add and it joins your watch list. The list is private to you; Amazon never sees it.

paragraphs.heading: Follow everything you already work with
paragraphs.text: Follow all brands I have content for follows every Creator Connections brand you already have content for, from your Storefront, Deals Butler and YouTube. One press and you are watching all of them.

paragraphs.heading: Follow as you accept
paragraphs.text: Automatically follow a brand when I accept its campaign keeps the list growing on its own. Any campaign you accept anywhere adds its brand here.

paragraphs.heading: The watch list
paragraphs.text: Everything you follow, with its live campaigns, best rate, the latest end date, and when it last alerted you. Unfollow removes it.

paragraphs.heading: Check now
paragraphs.text: Check now looks straight away. It also checks on its own a few times a day, whenever the central catalog refreshes. The first check after you follow a brand is quiet: it records what exists now so you only hear about new campaigns.

paragraphs.heading: How you hear about it
paragraphs.text: Alert methods: a popup in the app, a card on your Dashboard marked as needing attention, or an email. Pick any mix.

paragraphs.heading: Auto-accept
paragraphs.text: This is what gets you in early. Auto-accept new campaigns from brands I follow accepts their new campaigns for you. It is off until you turn it on, because accepting opts you in.

paragraphs.heading: Which ones, and how many
paragraphs.text: Which campaigns chooses all new campaigns, or only products you already have content for. Most to accept per check caps one check so it never grabs more than you want.

paragraphs.heading: By keyword, from any brand
paragraphs.text: You can also auto-accept by keyword from any brand: prime day, kitchen, back to school. Handy for a season you want to be in on.

paragraphs.heading: On a schedule
paragraphs.text: Run auto-accept on a schedule sets how often it checks and accepts, for example every six hours. Watch it run in the top bar shows the browser while it accepts.

paragraphs.heading: Next step
paragraphs.text: Your next step: press Follow all brands I have content for, turn on the Dashboard alert, and leave it a week before deciding on auto-accept.

E0e1-524es8.title: Walmart Research: Price And Rank History For Walmart Products

paragraphs.text: Is this Walmart deal really a deal, or is that just the normal price? Walmart Research keeps the history, so you can tell.

paragraphs.heading: Research library

paragraphs.heading: Track a product

paragraphs.heading: Check now

paragraphs.heading: Next step
paragraphs.text: Your next step: paste one Walmart product link above and press Add.

Ed8xZFBBotY.title: Influencer Butler Settings And Help: A Quick Tour

paragraphs.text: Every app has a Settings page. This one has thirteen sections, and three of them you will use a lot. Here is the tour.

paragraphs.heading: Appearance
paragraphs.text: Appearance. Language, light or dark theme, motion, zoom, and focus mode.

paragraphs.heading: Performance
paragraphs.text: Performance. On a small machine, Low resource mode runs automations one at a time so the window stays responsive.

paragraphs.heading: Profile
paragraphs.text: Profile. Your storefront ids and the accounts each platform signs in with.

paragraphs.heading: Show or Hide Butlers

paragraphs.heading: Notifications
