paragraphs.heading: Data and Backup
paragraphs.text: Data and Backup. Export everything, restore it, or move to a new computer.

paragraphs.heading: Updates
paragraphs.text: Updates install themselves when you quit. This section shows which version you are on and lets you check now.

paragraphs.heading: Pause all automations
paragraphs.text: Up in the top bar, Automations. One press pauses every schedule and every automatic run at once. Press it again to resume. Handy before a holiday.

paragraphs.heading: Help and Tutorials
paragraphs.text: Help and Tutorials. A written guide for every butler, with the video on top when there is one. Search finds a guide by name.

paragraphs.heading: Search the guides
paragraphs.text: Type a butler name or a question here.

paragraphs.heading: The AI assistant
paragraphs.text: The AI assistant answers in plain words and can take you to the right screen. Ask it how to do something, and it walks you there.

paragraphs.heading: Next step
paragraphs.text: Your next step: open Show or Hide Butlers and switch off the ones you do not need yet.

F0zedlQ9x5Y.title: Goldmine Butler: Find Brands That Already Pay Amazon Creators

paragraphs.heading: The shortcut to a pitch list
paragraphs.text: The easiest brands to pitch are the ones already paying someone like you. Goldmine Butler finds them by reading other creators' storefronts for sponsored posts.

paragraphs.heading: Power User feature
paragraphs.text: Quick note on plans. Goldmine Butler is a Power User feature. On the Beginner plan it is hidden from the sidebar. Upgrade any time in Settings, under Subscription.

paragraphs.heading: It only reads
paragraphs.text: It reads public storefront pages, the same ones you could open yourself, and looks up each product's brand. Nothing here messages anybody or touches your account.

paragraphs.heading: Storefronts to scan
paragraphs.text: Start with storefront links. Paste the Amazon storefront address of three to five creators in your own niche. Quality over quantity.

paragraphs.heading: Add another
paragraphs.text: Add another storefront adds a row.

paragraphs.heading: Keywords to match
paragraphs.text: Keywords keep it focused. Hashtag ad and hashtag partner are in by default. Add a narrow word for your niche and press Add, and only posts mentioning it are kept.

paragraphs.heading: Max items per storefront
paragraphs.text: Max items per storefront caps how many posts it reads per creator. The default is a hundred. Keep it low on the first run.

paragraphs.heading: Run
paragraphs.text: Run opens each storefront in the background and harvests the sponsored posts. It starts a fresh set of results each time, so export the last set first if it had something good.

paragraphs.heading: Scan totals
paragraphs.text: Four numbers: storefronts scanned, keyword matches, unique products, and unique brands. Brands is the one you care about.

paragraphs.heading: Hot leads
paragraphs.text: Then the leads: one row per sponsored post, with the creator it came from, the matched keyword, the product, the brand, and whether that brand has a Creator Connections or SPCC campaign open.

paragraphs.heading: Sort by brand
paragraphs.text: Click Brand Name to group them. A brand paying several creators in your niche is a higher-priority pitch.

paragraphs.heading: Send them on
paragraphs.text: Send to Group Invite Butler hands the leads over, and Export CSV takes them to a spreadsheet for your outreach.

paragraphs.heading: Next step
paragraphs.text: Your next step: five storefronts, one niche keyword, fifty posts each. Run it, sort by brand, and start pitching the brands that show up twice.

fIpsl8kimOs.title: Facebook Inviter: Turn Group Reactions Into Page Followers

paragraphs.heading: Reactions are wasted
paragraphs.text: You post a deal in a group. Forty people react. And then nothing, because none of them follow your Page. Facebook Inviter chases them up: it invites every one of those people to follow you.

paragraphs.heading: Power User feature
paragraphs.text: Quick note on plans. Facebook Inviter is a Power User feature. On the Beginner plan it is hidden from the sidebar. Upgrade any time in Settings, under Subscription.

paragraphs.heading: Every invite is real
paragraphs.text: It uses the same Facebook sign-in as Deals Butler, and every invite it sends is real, with no preview and no undo. So nothing is pressed today, and you start small.

paragraphs.heading: The master switch
paragraphs.text: Invite everyone who engaged with my posts is on by default. Turn it off to sit a run out.

paragraphs.heading: Your Page ID
paragraphs.text: The one required field: the numeric ID of the Page or profile people will be invited to follow. It is in your Page's About section or its address.

paragraphs.heading: Which account invites
paragraphs.text: Facebook account picks which signed-in account sends the invites. The list matches the accounts you set up in Deals Butler, so pick the one that owns the Page.

paragraphs.heading: Groups to skip
paragraphs.text: Skip these group IDs leaves out any group where you would rather not be seen inviting people.

paragraphs.heading: Max invites per post
paragraphs.text: Max invites per post is the cap that matters. Zero means everyone, which is not what you want on your first run. Ten is a sensible start.

paragraphs.heading: Scroll attempts
paragraphs.text: Scroll attempts per group decides how deep it digs into each group's feed. Ten is plenty.

paragraphs.heading: Watch it run
paragraphs.text: Watch it run in the top bar brings the browser on screen so you can see it work. It applies to every butler.

paragraphs.heading: Start
paragraphs.text: Start Facebook Inviter opens Chrome on that account, walks each group, opens the reaction lists on your posts, and presses Invite. The status badge reads Idle until then.

paragraphs.heading: Daily on autopilot
paragraphs.text: The scheduler plans a daily run: a start time, repeat every so many days, Enable Schedule.

paragraphs.heading: The results
paragraphs.text: Results count people invited, groups worked and posts opened, and list every run. Export CSV keeps a copy.

paragraphs.heading: Next step
paragraphs.text: Your next step: paste your Page ID, cap it at ten invites per post, and run it once while you watch.

fN26bxHT-bw.title: Fix Every Old Affiliate Link At Once: Relink Butler

paragraphs.heading: The day you switch
paragraphs.text: You change link provider, or you get a new tag. Every link you have ever posted is now the old one.

paragraphs.heading: Hundreds of posts
paragraphs.text: And they are scattered. Old deals posts, YouTube descriptions, Pinterest pins, Benable lists.

paragraphs.heading: This finds and swaps them
paragraphs.text: Relink Butler goes and finds them, works out the new version of each, and shows you before it changes anything.

paragraphs.heading: It is properly in beta
paragraphs.text: Read this bit. It is early, and in the normal installed app everything below is look but do not touch for now.

paragraphs.heading: Nothing has run
paragraphs.text: And this is the state. Idle. It only does something when you ask it to.

paragraphs.heading: Four kinds of swap
paragraphs.text: There are four jobs it can do, and picking the right one is most of the work.

paragraphs.heading: Changing link service
paragraphs.text: The first is changing service. You moved from one link shortener to another and want everything re-pointed.

paragraphs.heading: Changing your tag
paragraphs.text: The second is just your Amazon tag. Same links, different tag on the end.

paragraphs.heading: Type the new one
paragraphs.text: And that is where the new tag goes.

paragraphs.heading: Re-minting
paragraphs.text: The third builds brand new links through a network like Levanta, rather than editing the ones you have.

paragraphs.heading: Pick the network
paragraphs.text: You choose the network and the marketplace, and it mints fresh links for each product.

paragraphs.heading: Plain find and replace
paragraphs.text: And the fourth is the blunt one. Find this piece of text, put that instead. Useful when nothing else fits.

paragraphs.heading: Back to the common one
paragraphs.text: For most people the first option is the one. Let us put it back.

paragraphs.heading: Where to look
paragraphs.text: Now where. Four places it can search, and only your deals posts are ticked to start with.

paragraphs.heading: Start with deals only
paragraphs.text: Leave it that way for your first run. Deals is the only one it can change without opening a browser.

paragraphs.heading: The other three open Chrome
paragraphs.text: YouTube, Pinterest and Benable all need a real browser signed into your account to edit a published post.

paragraphs.heading: Preview changes nothing
paragraphs.text: Then Preview. This is the safe one. It reads, works out the swap, and writes nothing anywhere.

paragraphs.heading: Read the table
paragraphs.text: Afterwards you get a row per link. The old one on the left, the proposed one on the right.

paragraphs.heading: Nothing is pre-approved
paragraphs.text: And here is the thing to know. Nothing is ticked for you. You approve each row you want, one at a time.

paragraphs.heading: Then Apply
paragraphs.text: Apply only touches rows you approved. It stays greyed out until you have approved at least one.

paragraphs.heading: There is no going back
paragraphs.text: And there is no undo. The old link is overwritten in place. Nothing keeps a copy of it.

paragraphs.heading: What it will not fix
paragraphs.text: It also will not fix links to products that died, and it cannot see links you posted by hand outside the app.

paragraphs.heading: So, the order
paragraphs.text: Set up the new provider first. Then deals only, preview, read every row, approve a few, apply. Widen from there.

fOyidT7HXEI.title: Instagram Email Collection: Harvest Brand Emails Hiding in Your DMs

paragraphs.heading: It is in there somewhere
paragraphs.text: A brand said send your media kit to this address, three months ago, in a DM you cannot find. Instagram Email Collection scans your DM history and pulls every email address into a table.

paragraphs.heading: Power User feature
paragraphs.text: Quick note on plans. Instagram Email Collection is a Power User feature. On the Beginner plan it is hidden from the sidebar. Upgrade any time in Settings, under Subscription.

paragraphs.heading: It only reads
paragraphs.text: It opens your signed-in Instagram inbox and reads. It never sends anything. It does show your private inbox in the browser, so nothing is pressed today.

paragraphs.heading: Your numbers
paragraphs.text: Captured, marked sent, and pending outreach.

paragraphs.heading: Max threads to scan
paragraphs.text: Max threads to scan is how many DM threads it walks, newest first. Fifty is a good test; leave it empty to scan every thread.

paragraphs.heading: Incremental
paragraphs.text: Incremental only scans DMs newer than the last run, so later runs take seconds. Turn it off once for the first full backfill.

paragraphs.heading: Full message history
paragraphs.text: Full message history scrolls up in each thread to load older messages. Slower, exhaustive, use it once.

paragraphs.heading: Watch it run
paragraphs.text: Watch it run in the top bar keeps the browser on screen so you can see it walk the inbox. It applies to every butler.

paragraphs.heading: Run
paragraphs.text: Run opens Chrome on your Instagram session, opens each thread, and adds every email it finds to the table. A heavy inbox takes a few minutes the first time.

paragraphs.heading: On a schedule
paragraphs.text: The schedule runs it on a repeating interval, so new emails keep landing without you.

paragraphs.heading: The results
paragraphs.text: The results: one row per email with the username it came from, when it was captured, whether you marked it sent, and whether it is already in Pitch Butler. Filter by pitched status to see who is still waiting.

paragraphs.heading: Next step
paragraphs.text: Your next step: fifty threads, incremental off, press Run once. Then turn incremental on and put it on a weekly schedule.

HKGjjm76wrI.title: Amazon Deals: Find Discounts on Your Keywords and Turn Them Into Posts

paragraphs.heading: The daily grind
paragraphs.text: Find a good discount. Write a caption. Post it to a group, a channel, a page. Then do it all again tomorrow. Amazon Deals does the whole loop: it searches, it writes, and it queues.

paragraphs.heading: Included in the Beginner plan
paragraphs.text: Quick note on plans. Amazon Deals is included in the Beginner plan, so everyone has it.

paragraphs.heading: Store and hub
paragraphs.text: Amazon Deals is a store. Walmart Deals is its twin. Both post through the Deals Butler hub, which holds the destinations and the schedule. This panel decides what gets found and what the post says.

paragraphs.heading: Keywords
paragraphs.text: Start with Keywords. Monthly keyword batches hold the phrases each month's search rotates through, one per line. Suggest keywords by niche fills them with AI, and per-day keywords override a single date.

paragraphs.heading: Search Deals
paragraphs.text: Search Deals is the engine. It asks Amazon what is discounted right now on your keywords and fills the table below. Post per round decides how many Amazon then Walmart deals post when the stores take turns.

paragraphs.heading: The filter recipe
paragraphs.text: The filter recipe sets the hard limits: minimum percent off, price range, reviews, stars. Thirty percent off and a few hundred reviews is a sensible start.

paragraphs.heading: Promotion pages and auto-search
paragraphs.text: Two extras: pull deals from Amazon promotion pages, and Auto-search, which re-runs the search on a clock, every few hours or at a time of day.

paragraphs.heading: Run the search
paragraphs.text: Search Deals runs it. It uses the Creators API, and promotion pages open a signed-in Amazon window. The status badge says Ready when nothing is running. Not pressed today.

paragraphs.heading: What you get
paragraphs.text: The results: every deal with its discount, price, reviews, whether it has a Creator Connections campaign or an SPCC offer, and a send button. Select the good ones and send them to your posts.

paragraphs.heading: Build Your Post
paragraphs.text: Build Your Post is where you write the caption once. Pick a style and it fills the caption and first comment. The chips are placeholders: title, price, percent off, your link. Each deal fills them in when it posts.

paragraphs.heading: Variants
paragraphs.text: Caption variants rotate the wording so your feed does not repeat itself, and full-price posts get their own copy.

paragraphs.heading: The Deals queue
paragraphs.text: The Deals tab is the record: what is queued, what went out, and where each one landed.

paragraphs.heading: Always-Post and Add a Deal
paragraphs.text: Always-Post pins products that always carry a discount, so they post on their own schedule. Add a Deal hand-enters one a seller sent you, promo code and all.

paragraphs.heading: Promo codes and roundups
paragraphs.text: Promo Code Hub keeps the codes you attach to posts, and can scan your Creator Connections campaigns for them. Roundup Campaigns makes one Facebook post with the deals underneath as comments.

paragraphs.heading: Idea Lists
paragraphs.text: Idea Lists builds Amazon idea lists from your deals, Creator Connections products first, with AI-written descriptions, on the storefronts you pick.

paragraphs.heading: Settings
paragraphs.text: Settings holds this store's defaults: posting order, links, images, and Facebook pacing. Copy setup from another workspace brings a tuned store across.

paragraphs.heading: Next step
paragraphs.text: Your next step: five keywords for this month, a thirty percent floor, one caption style. Press Search Deals, send three deals to your posts, and let the hub schedule them.

hzAvn8ZJtsM.title: Sheetsyncer Butler: Send Your Butlers' Work to a Google Sheet

paragraphs.heading: The spreadsheet you keep anyway
paragraphs.text: You keep a spreadsheet of what the butlers did anyway, by hand. Sheetsyncer Butler fills it: connect a sheet once per source, choose the columns, and the rows flow.

paragraphs.heading: Power User feature
paragraphs.text: Quick note on plans. Sheetsyncer Butler is a Power User feature. On the Beginner plan it is hidden from the sidebar. Upgrade any time in Settings, under Subscription.

paragraphs.heading: Two sources
paragraphs.text: Two sources today, each on its own card: Facebook Group Builder posts, and Deals Butler, one card per deals workspace that searches.

paragraphs.heading: Group Builder posts
paragraphs.text: Group Builder: include the welcome, engagement and viral posts from your latest plan, one row per post with the caption and an image idea. Refresh pulls the latest plan.

paragraphs.heading: Connect a sheet
paragraphs.text: Connect opens the how-to: a sheet of yours, a small script you paste once, and the address it gives you. Then fetch the columns and match them to the fields.

paragraphs.heading: How to send
paragraphs.text: When sending: add new rows only, add every row, or replace all rows each time. Send trigger: manual, or automatic after new content is generated. Send to Google Sheet does it now.

paragraphs.heading: Deals Butler cards
paragraphs.text: The Deals Butler cards: Amazon Deals, Walmart Deals, each store and each clone gets its own sheet, and deals are sent automatically after each search once auto send is on in that store's Search Deals tab. Walmart can share Amazon's sheet.

paragraphs.heading: Copy the setup
paragraphs.text: Copy this setup to your other deals workspaces copies the column layout and options across; each keeps its own connected sheet.

paragraphs.heading: The live sheet
paragraphs.text: Paste a sheet link at the bottom and Show sheet embeds it right here, so you can read the rows without leaving the app.

paragraphs.heading: Next step
paragraphs.text: Your next step: connect one sheet to Amazon Deals, turn on auto send in its Search Deals tab, and watch the next search land as rows.

IZ1WanqNM38.title: Turn Deals Butler Finds Into A Benable List: Benable Deals

paragraphs.heading: What Benable Deals does
paragraphs.text: Your Deals Butler already has deals saved up. Putting them on a Benable list by hand is slow. This panel does it for you.

paragraphs.heading: Sign in to Benable first
paragraphs.text: First, sign in to Benable. The button then turns into a signed-in pill. You never type a name, because the app reads your account from your sign-in.

paragraphs.heading: Pick a Deals Butler
paragraphs.text: Pick a Deals Butler. The number in brackets is how many deals it holds. With two or more, you also get All Deals Butlers.

paragraphs.heading: Choose your stores
paragraphs.text: Choose your stores. Amazon is on. Walmart turns on only if that Deals Butler has Walmart deals.

paragraphs.heading: Choose a deal source
paragraphs.text: Deal source picks regular deals, Prime Day deals, or Walmart event deals. Each one keeps its own list below.

paragraphs.heading: Only show SPCC or Creator Connections
paragraphs.text: Only show narrows the regular deals you preview and post by hand to ones with an SPCC or Creator Connections campaign available. SPCC means Sponsored Products for Creators. The auto-run does not use it.

paragraphs.heading: Where should the deals go
paragraphs.text: Now choose where the deals go. Create a new public list, or refresh a list you already have.

paragraphs.heading: Name the new list
paragraphs.text: For a new list, type a clear title that tells people what is inside.

paragraphs.heading: Or paste an existing list link
paragraphs.text: To use a list you already have, paste its Benable link here. The auto-run uses this saved link.

paragraphs.heading: How many deals, and the caps
paragraphs.text: How many deals limits what you post by hand. Blank means all. The caps below start at 60 for a list and 80 in total.

paragraphs.heading: Preview before you post
paragraphs.text: Always preview first. Preview deals loads the hub's deals, and also adds them to the Items queue below.

paragraphs.heading: Every deal, as a card
paragraphs.text: Each card shows the photo, price, title, and ASIN, which is Amazon's product code. The bar below says how many loaded.

paragraphs.heading: Create list and publish
paragraphs.text: Create list and publish builds the list and makes it public, with no confirmation. If you are signed out, it opens sign-in first.

paragraphs.heading: Refresh adds, it does not replace
paragraphs.text: Pick Refresh an existing list, and the button says Refresh and publish. It adds deals and never deletes old ones. Deals already sent are skipped.

paragraphs.heading: The discount leads each note
paragraphs.text: Each deal's note leads with its discount, like 43% off, when it has one, with a fire emoji by default. You can turn that off or change the wording in List Publishing, under Advanced settings.

paragraphs.heading: The Items queue
paragraphs.text: Previewed deals also land in the Items queue. Each card shows the price, discount, status, and its target list, which stays blank until you set one.

paragraphs.heading: Select, set a list, publish
paragraphs.text: Select all ticks every card. Set target for selected picks their list. Publish selected sends them. A card with no list asks you for one.

paragraphs.heading: Remove and filter the queue
paragraphs.text: Remove from queue and Delete all only clear this queue, never Benable. Delete all asks you to confirm. Only show just hides cards.

paragraphs.heading: Auto-run keeps a list fresh
paragraphs.text: Auto-run is its own clock for this panel. Turn it on and it re-publishes your hub's current deals into your saved list.

paragraphs.heading: How often to run
paragraphs.text: Pick how often it runs: every 1, 3, 6, 12, or 24 hours.

paragraphs.heading: Custom: time and days
paragraphs.text: Custom lets you pick a time of day, every day or only certain days.

paragraphs.heading: What each auto-run does
paragraphs.text: Each run adds new deals first, then deletes what was already on the list from the bottom up, never below a minimum list size. An empty hub leaves your list alone.

paragraphs.heading: All Deals Butlers
paragraphs.text: Running several Deals Butlers? Pick All Deals Butlers. A card appears: one list for all of them, or one list for each.

paragraphs.heading: One list per Deals Butler
paragraphs.text: Each row gets a list name and a link. Leave the link empty and the list is created on the first update. Update all lists now starts refreshing them right away.

paragraphs.heading: Where it shows up next
paragraphs.text: Lists created here appear in Published Products, with Source set to Deals. Pick a Deals Butler and press Preview deals to start.

JSw7LUAt3E4.title: Influencer Butler Plans: Beginner vs Power User

paragraphs.heading: Two plans
paragraphs.text: Influencer Butler comes in two plans, Beginner and Power User. If a butler seems to be missing from your sidebar, this video explains why.

paragraphs.heading: Settings, then Subscription
paragraphs.text: Open Settings and pick Subscription. Your plan, your license key and your billing all live here.

paragraphs.heading: Your plan
paragraphs.text: This is your plan. Beginner includes the free butlers, Amazon Deals, Message Brands, Daily Commission Butler, the Reload butlers and Foyer, plus a monthly allowance of hosted AI so you do not need your own OpenAI key.

paragraphs.heading: Power User
paragraphs.text: Power User is everything: Walmart, Instagram, Facebook, Benable, the Goldmines, Collage, and the rest, with your own OpenAI key and one to one calls.

paragraphs.heading: Beginner Mode is different
paragraphs.text: One thing that trips people up. Beginner Mode, this button, only hides butlers to keep the sidebar simple. It does not change your plan. Everything comes back when you switch it off.

paragraphs.heading: Preview the Beginner plan
paragraphs.text: Preview Beginner plan is the real thing. It shows exactly what a Beginner account sees and can run. Your plan and billing do not change.

paragraphs.heading: What disappears
paragraphs.text: Look at the sidebar. Walmart Butler, Instagram, Facebook and the other Power User groups are gone. The Deals Butler group stays, because Amazon Deals is a Beginner feature.

paragraphs.heading: Switch back
paragraphs.text: Switch back to your plan and everything returns.

paragraphs.heading: Upgrading
paragraphs.text: To upgrade, press Switch plan right here. It swaps your subscription in place and charges only the difference. On a trial it simply switches which plan you are trying.

paragraphs.heading: Next step
paragraphs.text: Your next step: if a butler you want is missing, come to Subscription and press Switch plan.

KhWr6bJPZ-o.title: CC Check: Find and Accept Creator Connections Campaigns on Your Products

paragraphs.heading: Free money, if you ask
paragraphs.text: Brands run campaigns that pay extra on products you already talk about. CC Check finds every one that matches your products, and can accept them for you.

paragraphs.heading: Included in the Beginner plan
paragraphs.text: Quick note on plans. CC Check is included in the Beginner plan, so everyone has it.

paragraphs.heading: Give it your products
paragraphs.text: First it needs your products. Copy from Storefront Butler pulls in everything Storefront Butler already harvested, and Scan New Content picks up anything you posted since.

paragraphs.heading: Or import them
paragraphs.text: You can also paste product codes, upload a CSV, or fetch every Amazon product linked on a page of yours, like an old gift guide.

paragraphs.heading: Another creator's list
paragraphs.text: Two more ways in. Analyze list reads any creator's storefront or idea list and checks which of those products have a campaign. Check cart does the same for your Saved for later cart.

paragraphs.heading: Look first: Check Matches
paragraphs.text: Now the safe look. Check Matches compares your table against the cached catalog and shows what has a campaign. It accepts nothing and sends nothing.

paragraphs.heading: What you get
paragraphs.text: Three numbers: how many of your products a brand wants, how many have nothing yet, and how many campaigns are open.

paragraphs.heading: Check ASINs does more
paragraphs.text: Check ASINs is the full run. It checks every product against the live catalogs, accepts the campaigns that match, and submits your content links. Use it when you mean to say yes.

paragraphs.heading: Two switches that shape it
paragraphs.text: Include SPCC also opts you into Sponsored Products for Creators offers. Submit to best campaign only sends each product's link to the single best campaign instead of all of them.

paragraphs.heading: Watch it run
paragraphs.text: Watch it run in the top bar shows the browser while it accepts. It applies to every butler.

paragraphs.heading: Accept and submit on their own
paragraphs.text: Accept Campaigns and Submit Content do those two steps separately, and Sync Accepted History backfills anything you accepted on Amazon by hand.

paragraphs.heading: Read the table
paragraphs.text: The results table: the latest CC status, the SPCC status, whether it is accepted, the links you submitted, and whether content has posted. Filter by status to see only what is available.

paragraphs.heading: Send to the scheduler
paragraphs.text: Tick the rows you have already filmed and Send Selected to Auto Scheduler puts them in Deals Butler's Always-Post queue.

paragraphs.heading: On a schedule
paragraphs.text: Enable Schedule runs the check and accept on a timer. Learn the manual way first, then let it run.

paragraphs.heading: Next step
paragraphs.text: Your next step: copy from Storefront Butler, press Check Matches, and read the list. Press Check ASINs when you are ready to accept.

Kn6103GoQBA.title: Expired Butler: Clean Up Deal Posts After The Deal Ends

paragraphs.heading: Deals end. Posts keep running.
paragraphs.text: Every deal you post has a shelf life. When the sale ends, the post keeps sending people to a price that is gone. Expired Butler finds those posts and cleans them up.

paragraphs.heading: Included in the Beginner plan
paragraphs.text: A quick note on plans. Expired Butler is included in the Beginner plan, so everyone has it. It works on the posts Deals Butler made, on Facebook groups and pages, Telegram, Reddit and Threads.

paragraphs.heading: Pick your Facebook profile
paragraphs.text: Pick the Facebook profile that posted the deals. It is the same sign-in Deals Butler uses.

paragraphs.heading: Scan for expired
paragraphs.text: Scan for expired reads your posted deals and flags the ones whose end time has passed, or whose product is no longer on sale. It only finds and lists them. Nothing is removed yet.

paragraphs.heading: Found, selected, deleted, edited
paragraphs.text: The totals keep score. Expired posts found by the last scan, how many are selected for the next cleanup, and how many have been deleted or edited.

paragraphs.heading: Delete, or edit
paragraphs.text: Here is the key rule. A plain deal post is deleted. A post with a creator campaign attached is edited instead, so the campaign link stays live while the post stops advertising a dead price.

paragraphs.heading: The EXPIRED banner
paragraphs.text: This is the banner it adds to an edited post. Change the wording if you like, and choose whether it goes in the post itself or in a new comment.

paragraphs.heading: Maximum posts per run
paragraphs.text: Maximum posts per run is your safety cap. A cleanup never handles more than this in one go.

paragraphs.heading: Per-platform settings
paragraphs.text: Per-platform settings let one platform behave differently. Facebook groups could get the banner while Telegram only loses the code and dates.

paragraphs.heading: Schedule
paragraphs.text: The schedule sweeps for expired posts on its own, once a day by default. A scheduled run only reports what it would do until you turn on Let scheduled runs act automatically.

paragraphs.heading: Start small
paragraphs.text: The ramp starts small and grows a little each day, up to a maximum. Sleep hours keep it quiet overnight.

paragraphs.heading: History
paragraphs.text: History keeps a permanent record of everything deleted or edited. If a deal comes back on sale, Post again drops it into Deals Butler as a fresh draft.

paragraphs.heading: Clean up selected
paragraphs.text: When you are ready, tick the posts you want handled and press Clean up selected. Nothing is removed until you approve it.

paragraphs.heading: Next step
paragraphs.text: Your next step: pick your profile and press Scan for expired, then look over the list before you clean up.

ktfU-gayYFU.title: Orders Butler: Turn Your Amazon Orders Into a Filming List

paragraphs.heading: The daily question
paragraphs.text: You have hundreds of things in your house you already bought. Which one should you film today? Orders Butler answers that from your own order history.

paragraphs.heading: Included in the Beginner plan
paragraphs.text: Quick note on plans. Orders Butler is included in the Beginner plan, so everyone has it.

paragraphs.heading: It only reads
paragraphs.text: Orders Butler opens Amazon in your signed-in session and reads your order history. It never buys, never returns, and never touches anyone else's account.

paragraphs.heading: What it feeds
paragraphs.text: It is also the data feed for the rest of the Amazon group. Daily Commission Butler matches campaigns to these sales, and Earnings Intelligence builds its totals from them. Keep it fresh and everything downstream gets better.

paragraphs.heading: Block images
paragraphs.text: Block images for faster harvest stays on. It skips the pictures, and the read finishes much sooner.

paragraphs.heading: Only new since last run
paragraphs.text: Only new since last run is the everyday choice. It stops the moment it reaches orders it already has.

paragraphs.heading: The first time
paragraphs.text: The very first time, pick All years. It walks back to twenty thirteen, so it is slow, and you only do it once. Only fetch selected years is for filling in specific years later.

paragraphs.heading: Watch it run
paragraphs.text: Watch it run in the top bar decides whether the browser is visible. Leave it on for your first harvest so you can see it sign in and start walking pages. It applies to every butler.

paragraphs.heading: Run
paragraphs.text: Then press Run and leave it. A long history takes a while, so start it and go do something else. The status badge beside it tells you what it is doing.

paragraphs.heading: Your totals
paragraphs.text: Up top, the totals: orders harvested, what you spent, and how many products still need a photo, a vertical video, or a horizontal video.

paragraphs.heading: The table
paragraphs.text: Then the table. One row per product you bought: what you paid, what it earns, the commission rate, sales rank, how many influencer videos it already has, and whether it is on a deal right now.

paragraphs.heading: Film These First
paragraphs.text: Now the button to remember. Film These First sorts everything by what is worth your afternoon: products that pay well, that people are buying, and that hardly anyone has filmed.

paragraphs.heading: Tune the rule
paragraphs.text: The little gear lets you move the goalposts: max influencer videos, minimum commission, max sales rank, and bought per month. Reset to defaults puts the sensible numbers back.

paragraphs.heading: Just the gaps
paragraphs.text: Or filter to the gaps. Missing photo shows only the products you still have no photo for.

paragraphs.heading: Pick and print
paragraphs.text: Select the ones you want, then Print checklist makes a PDF of exactly what to shoot, with a box to tick as you go.

paragraphs.heading: Hand it to Content Butler
paragraphs.text: Send selected to Content Butler drops them on your content calendar, where the posts get written from what you filmed.

paragraphs.heading: Next step
paragraphs.text: Your next step: choose All years, press Run once, then press Film These First and go shoot.

kWJk-eQb6qI.title: Benable Comment Butler: AI Comments, Dry Run First

paragraphs.heading: A comment takes thought
paragraphs.text: A heart is quick. A comment takes thought. Comment Butler writes short comments on Benable list items for you.

paragraphs.heading: A Pro butler, maybe hidden
paragraphs.text: It is a Pro butler. If it is missing under Benable Butler, open Show / Hide Butlers and turn it on.

paragraphs.heading: Sign in to Benable first
paragraphs.text: Sign in to Benable here first. Watch it run, at the top, shows or hides the browser. Off and signed out, the run stops.

paragraphs.heading: The box that matters most
paragraphs.text: Dry run is ticked at first. Ticked, the butler writes comments but posts none. Unticked, it posts each comment to Benable for real, with no extra confirmation.

paragraphs.heading: Which profiles to visit
paragraphs.text: Add Benable profile links here, one per line. The butler walks every collection on each profile and looks at every item, until a cap stops it.

paragraphs.heading: Borrow your Like Butler list
paragraphs.text: Set up Like Butler already? This copies its profile list here, replacing what is in the box.

paragraphs.heading: Optional: Discover
paragraphs.text: Enable Discover mode to also scan Benable's Discover page. With no categories ticked, it scans the default Discover feed once.

paragraphs.heading: Pick Discover categories
paragraphs.text: There are 14 categories, and Trending is ticked at first.

paragraphs.heading: Amazon products only
paragraphs.text: Amazon-posted products only is the default. It opens each item and skips any with no Amazon link.

paragraphs.heading: Who writes the words
paragraphs.text: Mode picks who writes: AI plus canned fallback, the default, AI only, or canned only. AI only skips an item the AI cannot write.

paragraphs.heading: What the AI needs first
paragraphs.text: AI needs your OpenAI key, in AI and Data Keys. Without one, the default mode uses your canned phrases, and AI only will not start. If your Amazon Creators API is connected, the AI also reads each product's title and details.

paragraphs.heading: Your own canned phrases
paragraphs.text: Canned phrases go here, one per line. It picks one not yet used on that item, favoring ones not used this run.

paragraphs.heading: Length limits
paragraphs.text: AI comments must fit the length limits, 4 to 80 characters at first. It rejects any with a link, a question mark, an at-mention or a hashtag.

paragraphs.heading: Model and tone
paragraphs.text: The model starts as gpt-4o-mini. Tone is a short phrase that steers the writing. It starts as short, friendly, complimentary.

paragraphs.heading: Caps that keep it small
paragraphs.text: Per run is 5 and per day is 10 at first. Lifetime is 0. Zero means no limit, for per day and lifetime.

paragraphs.heading: Every Nth collection or item
paragraphs.text: Every Nth collection and item skip some on purpose. 1 means every one, and 3 means every third.

paragraphs.heading: A pause between comments
paragraphs.text: Delay between comments starts at 30 seconds, plus a random extra up to the jitter, 15 at first.

paragraphs.heading: Start with Dry run ticked
paragraphs.text: Start Comment Butler begins the run, and shows the browser if Watch it run is on. For a first run, leave Dry run ticked.

paragraphs.heading: Read what it wrote
paragraphs.text: In a dry run, each comment goes into a log file, marked not posted. The history table lists only posted comments, so open the log, or Download CSV.

paragraphs.heading: How the stats count
paragraphs.text: In a dry run, Comments this run counts what it wrote. Lifetime posted does not go up, and the per run cap still applies.

paragraphs.heading: After real posting
paragraphs.text: After real posting, the table shows each creator, how many comments were posted, and the latest comment's text.

paragraphs.heading: Careful clearing the log
paragraphs.text: Clear all asks first, and Undo last clear brings the log back. Careful: the log is how it remembers items it already commented on.

paragraphs.heading: Repeat on a schedule
paragraphs.text: Scheduler: Repeat every is in minutes, at least 15. Empty means once a day.

paragraphs.heading: Turn the schedule on
paragraphs.text: Enable Schedule turns it on. The first run is at the Start time, or one repeat interval from now if that is empty. Scheduled runs use your saved settings, Dry run included.

paragraphs.heading: Dry run first, then decide
paragraphs.text: So: run it dry, read every comment in the log, then untick Dry run, with small caps.

l_BlnRpQQOQ.title: Pitch Butler: One CRM for Every Brand Pipeline You Work

paragraphs.heading: Five inboxes, one pipeline
paragraphs.text: Outreach across Creator Connections, Levanta and Instagram means your pipeline lives in five places. Pitch Butler pulls them into one CRM: each brand is a card with its contacts, its deals, and every message you ever sent it.

paragraphs.heading: Power User feature
paragraphs.text: Quick note on plans. Pitch Butler is a Power User feature. On the Beginner plan it is hidden from the sidebar. Upgrade any time in Settings, under Subscription.

paragraphs.heading: Fill it
paragraphs.text: Fill it from the butlers: Import CC brands, Import Levanta emails, Instagram extract emails and scan posts, or Add brand, Paste emails and Import CSV. The Goldmines and Email Collections also send rows here.

paragraphs.heading: Send from your own email
paragraphs.text: Connect Gmail, or connect a custom email: Titan, Zoho, Outlook, Fastmail, or any SMTP host. Add the IMAP details and replies advance a brand's stage on their own. Your password is stored encrypted on this device.

paragraphs.heading: Filters
paragraphs.text: Filter by source, Creator Connections, Levanta, Instagram, Facebook, manual, and by status: prospect, pitched, replied, negotiating, closed, dead. Needs follow-up is the one to open every morning.

paragraphs.heading: Tags
paragraphs.text: Tags combine: awaiting approval, free sample, hot lead, follow up. Click one, or several.

paragraphs.heading: List, board, tasks, reports
paragraphs.text: Work it as a list, a drag-to-advance board, a task list with reminders, or the reports dashboard. The media kit tab holds what you send brands.

paragraphs.heading: Each brand card
paragraphs.text: Each brand card: the contact, where it came from, its status, and the message history that every workspace, Messenger included, rolls up into it.

paragraphs.heading: Copy prospect emails
paragraphs.text: Select all and Copy prospect emails hands a list to any email tool. Brand Pack bundles your pitch materials.

paragraphs.heading: Next step
paragraphs.text: Your next step: Import CC brands, connect your email, and open Needs follow-up. Pitch three brands today.

lak0Ggx3mH0.title: Instagram Like Butler: Auto-Like the Recent Posts of Accounts You Choose

paragraphs.heading: Being remembered
paragraphs.text: A steady like on a brand's or creator's posts is the cheapest way to stay on their radar without sending a message. Instagram Like Butler does the rounds for you.

paragraphs.heading: Included in the Beginner plan
paragraphs.text: Quick note on plans. Instagram Like Butler is included in the Beginner plan, so everyone has it.

paragraphs.heading: Real likes
paragraphs.text: These are real likes from your real account, and there is no unlike here, so nothing is started today.

paragraphs.heading: Instagram accounts
paragraphs.text: Instagram accounts: enter a username or profile link per row, each with its own optional max likes. Add another Instagram account adds a row. Five to ten accounts in your niche is a good list.

paragraphs.heading: Like every recent post
paragraphs.text: Like every recent post, on, likes posts seen on a previous run too. Off skips what it already liked. Leave it off.

paragraphs.heading: Max likes per run
paragraphs.text: Max likes per run is the budget across all accounts. Ten is the default.

paragraphs.heading: The delay
paragraphs.text: Delay between likes: eight to twelve seconds is safe, and Fast, Normal and Careful fill it for you. Faster than five seconds looks robotic.

paragraphs.heading: Recent posts per account
paragraphs.text: Recent posts per account is how many of the newest posts it checks on each profile.

paragraphs.heading: Watch it run
paragraphs.text: Watch it run in the top bar keeps the browser on screen for the first pass, and lets you sign in if Instagram asks. It applies to every butler.

paragraphs.heading: Start
paragraphs.text: Start Instagram Like Butler opens Chrome on your Instagram session, visits each account, and likes the recent posts. Pause holds it.

paragraphs.heading: On a schedule
paragraphs.text: The scheduler repeats it every so many minutes, and Only like during set hours keeps the likes inside a part of the day so they look human.

paragraphs.heading: History
paragraphs.text: History tracks what it liked, by creator, with the content type and the last activity. Download CSV keeps the log.

paragraphs.heading: Next step
paragraphs.text: Your next step: five accounts, ten likes, Careful speed. Run it once while you watch, then schedule it once a day inside your waking hours.

MdPYJyOtwb8.title: Video Reload Butler: Re-Upload Your Amazon Videos to Every Marketplace

paragraphs.heading: Filmed once, sold once
paragraphs.text: You filmed a product for the US storefront. That same video could be earning in Canada, the UK, Australia and Singapore, and a re-upload with a fresh title gets treated like a new post. Video Reload Butler does the copying.

paragraphs.heading: Included in the Beginner plan
paragraphs.text: Quick note on plans. Video Reload Butler is included in the Beginner plan, so everyone has it.

paragraphs.heading: It reads Storefront Butler
paragraphs.text: It reads your videos from the Storefront Butler table, so sync that first. And it publishes to your real storefronts, so nothing is run on camera today.

paragraphs.heading: Step 1: source and destinations
paragraphs.text: Five steps, top to bottom. Step one: Video source is the marketplace your videos live on, usually US. Upload destinations are where the copies go, each with its own sign-in.

paragraphs.heading: Start with one destination
paragraphs.text: Tick one destination on your first run and see how it lands. Amazon now cross-posts to some markets on its own, marked Amazon auto, so the others are where uploading yourself adds reach.

paragraphs.heading: Skip unavailable products
paragraphs.text: Skip products that are currently unavailable checks stock before uploading, so you never post a dead link.

paragraphs.heading: Step 2: preferred formulas
paragraphs.text: Step two starts with Preferred Formulas: one-click mixes for the common paths, like monetizable videos to the four markets, a US re-upload of short verticals, or reload my proven winners. Press one and every filter fills in.

paragraphs.heading: The formulas
paragraphs.text: Each formula has a question mark explaining what it sets. Everything stays editable afterwards.

paragraphs.heading: Timeframe and batch size
paragraphs.text: Timeframe narrows by date, and Max videos this run caps the batch. A handful the first time tells you whether you like the result.

paragraphs.heading: Quality guardrails
paragraphs.text: Quality guardrails keep your best work untouched: skip videos at or above a view count, skip below a minimum, or reload only videos above a minimum percent viewed.

paragraphs.heading: Step 3: transform
paragraphs.text: Step three transforms the video: convert to vertical, horizontal or square, trim or loop to a target length, join a clip, add a watermark, a caption, or an AI thumbnail.

paragraphs.heading: Run mode
paragraphs.text: Now the setting to read twice. Run mode decides what happens to the original. Post and keep original copies and leaves everything alone. The delete modes remove the original from Amazon.

paragraphs.heading: Winners first and fresh titles
paragraphs.text: Winners first reloads only videos whose products earned commissions. Refresh the title on reload gives each copy a new hook so Amazon treats it as a new post.

paragraphs.heading: Pace it
paragraphs.text: Minimum and maximum seconds between uploads, Limit uploads per day, and Warm up slowly keep a big library from going out all at once.

paragraphs.heading: Run
paragraphs.text: Run opens Chrome, converts each video, and uploads it to the destinations you ticked. Watch it run in the top bar keeps the browser on screen. The Video Log tab records every upload, and Deleted from Amazon keeps a local copy of anything removed.

paragraphs.heading: Next step
paragraphs.text: Your next step: one destination, max five videos, Post and keep original. Run it, check the Video Log, then pick a formula.

n-O15lU4dK8.title: The Influencer Butler Dashboard And Hub Dashboards

paragraphs.heading: Home

NEzqLWNX0gI.title: Walmart Photo Repost: Copy Your Amazon Storefront Photos To Walmart Creator

paragraphs.heading: Your Amazon photos, on Walmart too
paragraphs.text: You already made photos for your Amazon storefront. Walmart Creator wants photos too. Making them twice is not happening. Photo Repost copies them over for you.

paragraphs.heading: Power User feature
paragraphs.text: Quick note on plans. Photo Repost, like everything in the Walmart Butler group, is a Power User feature. On the Beginner plan the group is hidden. Upgrade any time in Settings, under Subscription.

paragraphs.heading: Set it up: sign in to Walmart
paragraphs.text: Set it up walks you through signing in to Walmart Creator. Sign in once. If you are signed out later, the run stops and asks you to sign in again.

paragraphs.heading: Only exact matches
paragraphs.text: Here is the rule. It only reposts a photo when the product is the exact same item on Walmart. Same barcode. Close is not good enough, so your photo never lands on the wrong product.

paragraphs.heading: Review first, then automatic
paragraphs.text: Posting has two modes. Review matches before posting shows you the matches and waits for you. Post matches automatically posts them on its own. Start with Review.

paragraphs.heading: Max to post per run
paragraphs.text: Max to post per run is your speed limit. Walmart does not publish a limit, so start small, around 5 to 8 a day, until your account has some history.

paragraphs.heading: Skip out-of-stock products
paragraphs.text: Skip out-of-stock products does what it says. No point sending people to an item they cannot buy.

paragraphs.heading: Automatic schedule
paragraphs.text: The schedule runs it for you. Repeat every so many hours or days, and pick a first run time. Apply schedule turns it on.

paragraphs.heading: Photo options
paragraphs.text: Photo options are optional. Add a watermark, on-screen text, or a QR code to the product. Photos must be JPG or PNG under 10 megabytes, or they are skipped with a reason.

paragraphs.heading: Exact Walmart matches
paragraphs.text: Down here are the matches. Each row is one of your storefront photos and the Walmart item it matched. In Review mode, this is the list you are approving.

paragraphs.heading: Filter by outcome
paragraphs.text: Show narrows the list to one outcome. Posted, failed, skipped, or not yet posted. Handy when you only want to see what went wrong.

paragraphs.heading: Post approved, Retry failed, Skip all
paragraphs.text: Post approved to Walmart sends the ones you approved. Retry failed tries the failed ones again. Skip all clears the list without posting anything.

paragraphs.heading: Needs Storefront Butler first
paragraphs.text: One thing it needs first. Storefront Butler. That is where your storefront photos come from. If it has never run, there is nothing to match, and this panel will tell you.

paragraphs.heading: Next step
paragraphs.text: Every post also shows up on the Walmart Butler hub. Your next step: run Storefront Butler, come back here, and press Start in Review mode.

NsGfXN-dx6w.title: Link Butler: Branded, Tracked Links That Open the Shopping App

paragraphs.heading: Included in the Beginner plan
paragraphs.text: Quick note on plans. Link Butler is included in the Beginner plan, so everyone has it.

paragraphs.heading: Your numbers

paragraphs.heading: Paste a product link
paragraphs.text: Create a Butler Link: paste the product link. It reads the product so you recognise it at a glance.

paragraphs.heading: Title and campaign
paragraphs.text: A title only you see, and a campaign so its clicks group together in Performance.

paragraphs.heading: Add Butler Link
paragraphs.text: Add Butler Link mints the Calling Card. It is live the moment it is made, so I am not pressing it here. Add several at once takes one product link per line.

paragraphs.heading: The ledger
paragraphs.text: Your Butler Links is the ledger: the product, the Calling Card with one-click copy, where it was posted, a two-week click trend, total clicks, a health pill that reads Live, Healed or Broken, and your notes and tags.

paragraphs.heading: Search and filter
paragraphs.text: Search, filter by health, posted or not, retailer, campaign or tag, and Group by campaign for subtotals. Export Ledger takes it to a spreadsheet.

paragraphs.heading: QR Studio
paragraphs.text: QR Studio turns any link into a QR code with your colors and logo, for packaging, print or a story.

paragraphs.heading: Make one
paragraphs.text: Paste a link, pick the colors, and download it as PNG or SVG.

paragraphs.heading: Performance
paragraphs.text: Performance charts the taps over time, by link and by campaign, so you know which placements earn.

paragraphs.heading: Settings
paragraphs.text: Settings holds your default affiliate tag, link routing and providers like Mavely, and your own custom domain. It saves as you type.

paragraphs.heading: Next step
paragraphs.text: Your next step: paste one product link, add it, copy the Calling Card, and share it in your next post. Come back in a day and read the clicks.

nVjf9eA4-mk.title: Black Friday Butler: Never Miss A Time-Limited Deal On Your Storefront

paragraphs.heading: Deals move fast
paragraphs.text: A Black Friday price on one of your products might last four hours. If you miss it, you miss the post. This one just watches, and writes it down.

paragraphs.heading: Power User feature
paragraphs.text: Quick note on plans. Black Friday Butler is a Power User feature. On the Beginner plan it is hidden from the sidebar. Upgrade any time in Settings, under Subscription.

paragraphs.heading: It only logs
paragraphs.text: Despite the name, there is no posting here. It reads your own storefront on a timer and logs anything flagged as a deal, with a timestamp. Posting is Deals Butler's job.

paragraphs.heading: Your storefront link
paragraphs.text: One thing to fill in: the public link to your own Amazon storefront.

paragraphs.heading: How often to look
paragraphs.text: How often to look. From every 5 minutes to every 7 days. In a normal week, daily is plenty. On the sale weekend, go tight.

paragraphs.heading: Is it running?
paragraphs.text: Status, last run and next run, so you always know what it is doing.

paragraphs.heading: Deals surfaced
paragraphs.text: Every deal it found, with the time it saw it. Export CSV or Copy table takes the list to a spreadsheet or straight into a post.

paragraphs.heading: Start run
paragraphs.text: Start run begins the watch. Watch it run in the top bar shows the browser working; turn it off to run quietly.

paragraphs.heading: Next step
paragraphs.text: Your next step: paste your storefront link, pick daily, and press Start run.

nX_ab1hxdYw.title: Levanta Email Extractor: Build a Brand Contact List While You Pitch

paragraphs.heading: Power User feature

paragraphs.heading: Your numbers
paragraphs.text: Captured, marked sent, pending outreach, and unique brands.

paragraphs.heading: Filter
paragraphs.text: Filter by brand or email, and by pitched status, to see who is still waiting for a message.
