paragraphs.text: Your next step: run Message Brands once, then come back here, mark the brands you emailed as sent, and send the rest to Pitch Butler.

O7MFp8d--YE.title: Keywords and Filters: Tell Message Brands Who to Contact, Plus AI Keywords for the Year

paragraphs.heading: Every message starts here
paragraphs.text: Every brand Message Brands contacts for you starts on this screen. This is where you say what you want to be sent, and what you never want.

paragraphs.heading: Included in the Beginner plan
paragraphs.text: Quick note on plans. Keywords and Filters is included in the Beginner plan, so everyone has it.

paragraphs.heading: Keywords or brand name
paragraphs.text: Type a product type or a brand name and press Add. Each becomes a chip. Only campaigns matching one of these get a message. Leave it empty and everything qualifies.

paragraphs.heading: Chips you can pause and reorder
paragraphs.text: Disable pauses a chip without deleting it. Drag to reorder, and the first matching keyword runs first. Keyword Packs drops in a ready-made set for a niche.

paragraphs.heading: What to skip
paragraphs.text: Underneath are the skip lists, with a toggle to fold them away. Any campaign with one of these words in its title is skipped.

paragraphs.heading: Words you never film
paragraphs.text: Good ones here are things you would never film: supplements, vape, anything off limits for you.

paragraphs.heading: Brands to skip
paragraphs.text: And brands to skip takes a brand out entirely. A competitor, or somebody you already work with directly. A skip always beats an include.

paragraphs.heading: The AI half
paragraphs.text: Now the clever half. Describe what you sell and the AI writes a year of keywords, one list per month, ranked against the campaign catalog so the ones with live campaigns sort first.

paragraphs.heading: Who buys from you
paragraphs.text: Target audience is optional but it helps. Busy parents get different ideas than college students.

paragraphs.heading: Price range
paragraphs.text: The price range is a real filter: suggestions outside it are dropped. The minimum ships at thirty, so lower it if you sell cheaper products.

paragraphs.heading: Steer the ideas
paragraphs.text: These tick boxes steer the suggestions: trending, bought in multiples, solves a problem, giftable, and so on.

paragraphs.heading: Add to existing
paragraphs.text: Add to existing matters. Tick it and a new run adds to your months instead of replacing them.

paragraphs.heading: Generate all months
paragraphs.text: Generate all months writes the twelve lists using your OpenAI key, or the hosted AI on the Beginner plan. It costs pennies a run.

paragraphs.heading: Twelve boxes
paragraphs.text: The payoff: twelve boxes, one per month, each full of things worth chasing at that time of year. They are plain text, so edit anything.

paragraphs.heading: Send to Message Brands
paragraphs.text: When a month looks right, send it to Message Brands. That is the list your outreach works from. Copy settings from Deals Butler pulls in that butler's setup and replaces every month, so use it on purpose.

paragraphs.heading: Next step
paragraphs.text: Your next step: add three keywords you want, three words you never want, drop the price floor to ten, and generate your year.

OsXypHthbec.title: Benable List Optimize: Score and Fix Your Lists

paragraphs.heading: Polishing lists by hand
paragraphs.text: A Benable profile with dozens of lists is a lot to polish by hand. List Optimize scores your lists, and can fix them for you.

paragraphs.heading: A Pro butler, signed in
paragraphs.text: It is a Pro butler, which needs a Pro subscription after your free trial, and it works through your Benable account. Sign in here first, or nothing can be written to your lists.

paragraphs.heading: What you need first
paragraphs.text: For AI-written fixes, you need your OpenAI key in AI and Data Keys. To add products, your Amazon Creators API must be connected. Scanning and scoring need neither.

paragraphs.heading: Your profile link
paragraphs.text: Paste your Benable profile link here. It is saved.

paragraphs.heading: Scan without changing anything
paragraphs.text: Just scan reads and scores the lists on your profile, up to 100 of them. It changes nothing and costs no AI credits.

paragraphs.heading: The whole-profile run
paragraphs.text: Optimize my whole profile does the work. It asks first, because it writes to your live Benable account and spends AI credits. A Stop button appears while it runs.

paragraphs.heading: What it does to each list
paragraphs.text: Lists already marked Optimized are left alone. For the rest, it can rewrite a weak title or description, fill empty section descriptions, and add products to thin lists. By default it also adds non-product picks and can create new non-product lists, which we cover next.

paragraphs.heading: Uses List Publishing settings
paragraphs.text: Added products follow your List Publishing settings, including marketplace, minimum rating and reviews, and item target.

paragraphs.heading: A guided tour
paragraphs.text: Show me how gives a short guided tour.

paragraphs.heading: Open the one-list tool
paragraphs.text: To work on one list, open Optimize just one list.

paragraphs.heading: Audit one list
paragraphs.text: Paste a list link, then press Audit list. It scores the list with no AI cost.

paragraphs.heading: Fold it away again
paragraphs.text: That is the single-list tool.

paragraphs.heading: Non-product balance
paragraphs.text: Non-product balance mixes in picks that are not products, like local places, tutorials and apps. This switch is on at first.

paragraphs.heading: Add picks to product lists
paragraphs.text: During a sweep, this adds up to 2 non-product picks to the all-product lists it is optimizing, skipping any that already have some.

paragraphs.heading: Create new non-product lists
paragraphs.text: This can create new non-product lists when fewer than 30 percent of your lists have non-product picks. It needs OpenAI.

paragraphs.heading: How many new lists
paragraphs.text: New lists per run starts at 2 and goes up to 10. It never auto-creates more than 10 in total.

paragraphs.heading: Payout preferences
paragraphs.text: Payout preferences are off at first. Favor the highest-paying retailers, or the longest cookie windows, to lean toward better partner stores. Advertised rates are not guarantees.

paragraphs.heading: How a swap works
paragraphs.text: When it swaps an item, it adds the new one first, and removes the old one only on an exact match. Amazon items are never removed. Swaps need OpenAI.

paragraphs.heading: Schedule: profile and cadence
paragraphs.text: Auto-optimize on a schedule. Add the profile link, then pick how often: a number, and hours or days. The default is every 1 day.

paragraphs.heading: Spread the start time
paragraphs.text: Spread the start time adds a random delay, so runs do not all land at the same moment.

paragraphs.heading: Scheduled runs write live
paragraphs.text: Turn on automatic optimizing arms the schedule. Scheduled runs work in the background, with no confirmation, and write to your live lists. Stay signed in.

paragraphs.heading: Run once now
paragraphs.text: Run once now does one of those background runs right away, also with no confirmation.

paragraphs.heading: Score and Optimized badge
paragraphs.text: After an audit, you get an Optimization score from 0 to 100, the app's own signal, and an Optimized badge read from your Benable profile.

paragraphs.heading: Why it scored that way
paragraphs.text: The score has 8 categories, like Title and Product notes. Click one to see the facts behind its score.

paragraphs.heading: Section descriptions
paragraphs.text: Section descriptions picks AI-written text for each section, or a simple template line.

paragraphs.heading: Generate AI fixes
paragraphs.text: Generate AI fixes writes replacement copy with OpenAI. It spends credits, and results are saved per list so a re-audit does not spend again.

paragraphs.heading: Add products
paragraphs.text: Add products tops up the list using your List Publishing settings. It asks first.

paragraphs.heading: Auto-improve this list
paragraphs.text: Auto-improve this list does it in one go. It writes the AI fixes first, which spends credits, then asks before it applies the safe fixes to your live list. It only rewrites a title or description that needs it.

paragraphs.heading: Ready-to-use fixes
paragraphs.text: Ready-to-use fixes have Copy and, when possible, Apply to list. Undo puts back the last title or description change. New sections and product notes are copy and paste only.

paragraphs.heading: Least optimized first
paragraphs.text: After a scan, your lists show here, least optimized first. Which lists picks the group to optimize, and Optimized lists are left out.

paragraphs.heading: Recent audits
paragraphs.text: Recent audits keeps your latest audits. Click a row to audit that list again.

paragraphs.heading: Start with a scan
paragraphs.text: Start with Just scan, and read the scores. Then try the whole-profile run on a profile you are happy to have changed.

plZS_nXX-BE.title: Influencer Butler Creator Api Integration Setup Tutorial

paragraphs.heading: Why you need Creator API credentials
paragraphs.text: Hey guys, in order for Influencer Butler to run correctly across the workspaces and make everything so much easier for you and your butler, you are going to create an application in the Creators API section of your Amazon Influencer account. Simply go to the Tools section and click on Creators API.

paragraphs.heading: Create the app
paragraphs.text: Here you can create an app. You can name it whatever you want. Then you click Create. Then you want to add a new credential.

paragraphs.heading: Download and copy the credential
paragraphs.text: The first thing you should do is download it and save it to your computer. Then you are going to copy this credential ID. Bring up your Influencer Butler API Integrations and put the ID here.

paragraphs.heading: The secret key and version
paragraphs.text: Then go back, grab the secret key, and take note of the version shown. It will probably be version 2.1 for a long time. Go back to your Influencer Butler, paste the secret key, then select the version we were just talking about, 2.1.

paragraphs.heading: Marketplace and storefront ID
paragraphs.text: Currently we have the ability to integrate into the APIs for all marketplaces. I am going to select US. Here your tag should be pre-populated. If not, you can enter it. This is the storefront ID you want to use, the one that gives you access to your storefront for your Amazon Influencer account. It is not your onsite ID, which starts with O N A M Z.

paragraphs.heading: Test the connection
paragraphs.text: Then you want to test the connection and make sure it is connected. Then you are all set. If it is not connected, double check that you copied and pasted these keys correctly. If it still fails, email us at hello@influencerbutler.com for additional support. Now you can move on to the next step.

q9APiWH0des.title: Storefront Butler: Sync Your Whole Amazon Storefront Into One Table

paragraphs.heading: Do this one first
paragraphs.text: If you set up one thing today, make it this one. Most of the Amazon butlers read from what Storefront Butler finds: Video Reload, Photo Reload, Retag, Benable, CC Check. Empty here means empty there.

paragraphs.heading: Included in the Beginner plan
paragraphs.text: Quick note on plans. Storefront Butler is included in the Beginner plan, so everyone has it.

paragraphs.heading: What it does
paragraphs.text: It opens your Amazon storefront in your signed-in session and writes down everything on it: every video, every photo, every idea list and media list, and every product tagged in them. Then it looks each product up for price, deal and stock.

paragraphs.heading: Nothing to paste
paragraphs.text: There is no address to paste. It already knows your storefront from Settings. A Creators API key is recommended for prices and commission rates, but the scan runs without one.

paragraphs.heading: Discovery switches
paragraphs.text: Two optional discovery switches: Related CC campaign discovery also notes the Creator Connections campaigns on your products, and Related products discovery pulls in the products Amazon shows beside yours.

paragraphs.heading: Watch it run
paragraphs.text: Watch it run in the top bar shows the browser while it reads. Turn it off and it works quietly in the background. It applies to every butler.

paragraphs.heading: Run
paragraphs.text: Then Run. It reads your storefront one section at a time, and you can stop any time without losing what it already found.

paragraphs.heading: Content totals
paragraphs.text: The totals count up as it goes: videos, photos, idea lists, media lists, and products. This is the part you came for.

paragraphs.heading: The results table
paragraphs.text: Then the table. One row per product on your storefront, with the content it sits in, the price, the deal, the commission rate, whether it has a Creator Connections campaign, and whether it is still in stock.

paragraphs.heading: Search
paragraphs.text: Search narrows it by keyword or product code.

paragraphs.heading: What is out of stock
paragraphs.text: The ASIN Status filter is worth checking weekly. Out of stock shows the products nobody can buy any more, which is exactly what Retag Butler fixes.

paragraphs.heading: Keep prices fresh
paragraphs.text: Update Pricing and Deals refreshes prices and deals for every row, and Auto-refresh does it every six, twelve or twenty-four hours.

paragraphs.heading: Send it on
paragraphs.text: Send selected to Benable Butler queues rows for a Benable list, and Export CSV takes the whole table to a spreadsheet.

paragraphs.heading: Next step
paragraphs.text: Your next step: press Run once and let it finish. Then come back weekly, filter to Out of stock, and let the other butlers work from a fresh table.

QZJTipWsZnM.title: Pricecrash Butler: Catch Amazon Pricing Errors Before They Are Fixed

paragraphs.heading: The best post you can make
paragraphs.text: A ninety-nine percent off pricing mistake is the best thing you can post. It sells out in an hour. The trouble is finding it before the seller does. Pricecrash Butler is the radar.

paragraphs.heading: Power User feature
paragraphs.text: Quick note on plans. Pricecrash Butler is a Power User feature. On the Beginner plan it is hidden from the sidebar. Upgrade any time in Settings, under Subscription.

paragraphs.heading: Your numbers
paragraphs.text: Deals found in the last run, the average discount, how many are waiting for your review, and how many posted on their own.

paragraphs.heading: Minimum discount
paragraphs.text: Minimum discount is the whole tool. Ninety-nine catches genuine mistakes only. Lower it to seventy-five or eighty-five and you widen the net to clearance and overstock.

paragraphs.heading: When a deal is found
paragraphs.text: The setting that decides what happens next. Draft for review lands it in Deals Butler for you to approve. Auto-schedule posts it, right away or at your next scheduled time. No hand-off just logs it here. Start with Draft.

paragraphs.heading: Send finds to
paragraphs.text: Send finds to chooses which Deals Butlers receive each catch, so one pricing error can go out to more than one audience.

paragraphs.heading: Sources
paragraphs.text: Sources: Amazon, Walmart, and Target. Tick the stores you post from.

paragraphs.heading: Categories
paragraphs.text: Categories narrow the sweep. Select all casts wide; a few that match your niche is faster and cleaner.

paragraphs.heading: Marketplaces
paragraphs.text: Marketplaces to scan adds other Amazon countries once their Creators API credentials are connected in Settings. Start with one.

paragraphs.heading: Bait keywords
paragraphs.text: Bait keywords are the giveaway words: clearance, open box, closeout, overstock. Add your own.

paragraphs.heading: Run it on a clock
paragraphs.text: Run automatically sweeps on an interval. Do not re-post the same deal for a window keeps one catch from going out twice, and the limits cap posts per run, per hour and per day.

paragraphs.heading: Email me
paragraphs.text: Email me a summary after each run tells you what it caught without opening the app.

paragraphs.heading: Run
paragraphs.text: Run starts a sweep now. In Draft mode nothing is published; it waits for you in Deals Butler. Watch it run in the top bar shows the browser when one opens.

paragraphs.heading: The results
paragraphs.text: The results table lists every catch with its price, the discount, the store, and where it was sent.

paragraphs.heading: Next step
paragraphs.text: Your next step: ninety-nine percent, Draft for review, your niche categories, one marketplace. Run it once and see what it finds.

RdM4F9NyB7c.title: AI and Data Keys: Connect OpenAI, Keepa, Fal and Ideogram Once for Every Butler

paragraphs.heading: One panel, every key
paragraphs.text: Voiceover, Group Builder, the AI images, Product Research backfills: each needs a key. Instead of asking inside every butler, AI and Data Keys takes them once.

paragraphs.heading: Included in the Beginner plan
paragraphs.text: Quick note on plans. AI and Data Keys is included in the Beginner plan, so everyone has it. On the Beginner plan the hosted AI covers a monthly allowance with no key at all; your own key always wins.

paragraphs.heading: OpenAI
paragraphs.text: OpenAI first. One key powers the script writing, the captions and the AI images. Your key calls OpenAI directly and they bill your account, so the numbers here are estimates.

paragraphs.heading: Chat model
paragraphs.text: Chat model picks the model Voiceover Butler writes with: best quality, balanced, fast, or cheapest.

paragraphs.heading: Usage and spend cap
paragraphs.text: Usage this month: calls and estimated spend, by model. The soft spend cap warns you past a number; it never blocks a call, so set a hard cap in your OpenAI account if you need one.

paragraphs.heading: Test Connection
paragraphs.text: Test Connection proves a key works and remembers when it was last tested. Run saved tests on startup re-checks every stored key when the app opens.

paragraphs.heading: Keepa
paragraphs.text: Keepa is optional: with a key, Product Research backfills a product's full price and rank history the first time you look at it.

paragraphs.heading: Fal and Ideogram
paragraphs.text: Fal is the cheapest provider for photographic AI images, and Ideogram the strongest for text inside images. AI Content Butler routes each style to the one that is connected and falls back to OpenAI.

paragraphs.heading: The rest
paragraphs.text: YouTube Data, Google Places and Etsy keys sit below for the butlers that use them. Keys are stored encrypted on this computer.

paragraphs.heading: Next step
paragraphs.text: Your next step: paste your OpenAI key, press Test Connection, and set a soft cap you would want to hear about.

sJp1xmNSm7g.title: See Every Product You Published To Benable: Published Products

paragraphs.heading: Which products did you publish
paragraphs.text: Benable Butler publishes lists for you. But which products ended up in them, and why did it pick each one? Published Products answers that.

paragraphs.heading: A record of what was published
paragraphs.text: It fills up when Benable Butler creates a list, from List Publishing or from Benable Deals. It is a record of what was published, not a live copy of your Benable lists.

paragraphs.heading: The five totals
paragraphs.text: These five cards count everything published: total, SPCC sponsored, Creator Connections, from Amazon, and no campaign. Your filters never change them.

paragraphs.heading: Reason: why it was picked
paragraphs.text: Reason is why a product was picked. It might say SPCC sponsored, Creator Connections, On sale, or Niche match. Hover the chip to see every reason.

paragraphs.heading: CC and SPCC columns
paragraphs.text: CC and SPCC show whether a product has a Creator Connections campaign or a Sponsored Products for Creators offer. A small badge says accepted or not accepted.

paragraphs.heading: SPCC link check
paragraphs.text: SPCC link checks whether the link in your list is the right accepted SPCC link. It says Not checked until you run Check links or Fix links, under Fix SPCC links in List Publishing.

paragraphs.heading: Commission
paragraphs.text: Commission shows the campaign rate. With no campaign, an Amazon product can show the standard rate, marked std.

paragraphs.heading: Ends: campaign status
paragraphs.text: Ends gives the campaign end date with a tag: Active, Ending soon, or Ended. Ending soon means within 7 days. Ongoing means no end date was found, and No campaign means nothing is tied to the product.

paragraphs.heading: Source: List Publishing or Deals
paragraphs.text: Source tells you whether List Publishing or a Deals run made it. Click the heading to sort, so the Deals products sit together.

paragraphs.heading: Where each product lives
paragraphs.text: Collection, List, and Section show where each product lives. Click a list name to open the live list on Benable.

paragraphs.heading: Published date and status
paragraphs.text: Published is the date Benable Butler added the product. Status says Published, or Failed if it never reached the list.

paragraphs.heading: Search
paragraphs.text: Search finds a product by its name, ASIN, caption, list, or collection.

paragraphs.heading: Filter the table
paragraphs.text: The dropdowns narrow by collection, list, CC, SPCC, reason, campaign status, and retailer. The count above the table shows how many rows are left.

paragraphs.heading: Export what you see
paragraphs.text: Export CSV saves the rows your filters leave, in your current sort order. So a filtered view exports filtered.

paragraphs.heading: Delete only hides rows
paragraphs.text: Delete selected and Delete all shown only hide rows here. Nothing is removed from Benable. Show hidden lets you see them and restore them.

paragraphs.heading: Refresh after you publish
paragraphs.text: After List Publishing or Benable Deals creates a new list, come back and press Refresh to load its products.

UarNACgaH7Y.title: Walmart Butler Hub Tour: Every Walmart Butler On One Screen

paragraphs.heading: One screen for every Walmart butler
paragraphs.text: You have half a dozen Walmart butlers to keep an eye on. Checking each one is a chore. This hub puts them all on one screen.

paragraphs.heading: Power User feature
paragraphs.text: Quick note on plans. Everything in the Walmart Butler group is a Power User feature. On the Beginner plan this whole group is hidden. If you cannot find it, that is why. Upgrade any time in Settings, under Subscription.

paragraphs.heading: Today's numbers
paragraphs.text: Today's numbers. The big one is Walmart deals posted. The small arrows show how today compares with yesterday, and each number has a tiny chart behind it.

paragraphs.heading: Activity chart
paragraphs.text: The activity chart shows posted, failed and skipped over time. Pick today, 7, 30 or 90 days, and switch between by activity and by butler.

paragraphs.heading: Up next
paragraphs.text: Up next is what the planner will run in the next 24 hours, and when. A butler on a schedule shows up here before it starts.

paragraphs.heading: Butlers in this group
paragraphs.text: Every Walmart butler gets a card. Walmart Deals, Video Repost, Photo Repost, Collection Builder, Walmart Research, Performance and Settings. A second Deals Butler shows up here too. Below, Recent activity lists each run as it finishes.

paragraphs.heading: Open, Run, Watch the tutorial
paragraphs.text: Each card has Open and Run. Open jumps to that butler's panel. Run starts it from right here. Watch the tutorial plays the video for that butler, so help is one click away.

paragraphs.heading: A quick look at the Beginner plan
paragraphs.text: Now a quick look at the Beginner view, so the two plans make sense. Open Settings and find Subscription.

paragraphs.heading: Preview Beginner plan
paragraphs.text: Preview Beginner plan switches the app to what a Beginner account sees. Nothing about your plan or billing changes. It is only a preview.

paragraphs.heading: The Walmart group is hidden
paragraphs.text: Look at the sidebar. The whole Walmart Butler group is gone. The Deals Butler group is still there, because Amazon Deals is part of the Beginner plan. Walmart Deals is not.

paragraphs.heading: Switch back to your plan
paragraphs.text: Switch back, and everything returns. A real Beginner account can upgrade right here on the Subscription page.

paragraphs.heading: Back on the hub
paragraphs.text: Back on the hub. Your next step: press Watch the tutorial on any card and set that butler up.

upRAOn8Ebdk.title: Voiceover Butler: FTC-Compliant Video Scripts From Any ASIN

paragraphs.heading: The blank page
paragraphs.text: You know the product and you have the camera. The script is the part that stalls. Voiceover Butler writes it from the product's details, vetted against Amazon's video rules, with the disclosure built in.

paragraphs.heading: Power User feature
paragraphs.text: Quick note on plans. Voiceover Butler is a Power User feature. On the Beginner plan it is hidden from the sidebar. Upgrade any time in Settings, under Subscription.

paragraphs.heading: What it needs
paragraphs.text: Every Generate is a paid OpenAI call on your key from Settings, under API Integrations, and the product details come from the Creators API. Orders Butler can also send selected products straight here.

paragraphs.heading: Add products
paragraphs.text: Add products: paste ASINs one per line, or describe an off-Amazon product. Notes steer the angle, and the timeline says what is shown in the video and when.

paragraphs.heading: Brand guidelines
paragraphs.text: Brand-supplied guidelines: paste the brief the brand sent, or load it from a PDF, and the script treats it as binding on top of Amazon's rules.

paragraphs.heading: Length and video type
paragraphs.text: Script options travel with each job. Length, fifteen to sixty seconds. Video type: social hook, tutorial, unboxing, problem and solution, educational, product setup.

paragraphs.heading: Hook, pacing, disclosure
paragraphs.text: The opening hook, a joke, a relatable scenario, a bold claim, a question. Pacing. And the FTC disclosure: honest paid sample, affiliate link, free PR sample, or organic.

paragraphs.heading: Add to queue
paragraphs.text: Add to queue makes a job per ASIN with these options. Import CSV adds many at once.

paragraphs.heading: Jobs
paragraphs.text: Jobs: the product, its status, how many scripts it has, and when it was updated. Filter by status, select the ones you want, and Generate selected writes them. Not pressed today.

paragraphs.heading: View and star
paragraphs.text: View opens the scripts for a product. Generate another writes a fresh take. Star the one you like, and the Orders Butler checklist prints it.

paragraphs.heading: Next step
paragraphs.text: Your next step: one ASIN, thirty seconds, a relatable hook, the right disclosure. Add to queue, generate, and read it out loud.

VHKGyOuIGCA.title: Walmart Deals: Find And Post Walmart Deals Automatically

paragraphs.heading: Walmart deals, posted for you
paragraphs.text: Walmart runs deals all day long. Finding them and posting them by hand eats your evening. Walmart Deals does that work for you.

paragraphs.heading: Power User feature
paragraphs.text: About plans. Amazon Deals is included in the Beginner plan. Walmart Deals is a Power User feature. On Beginner, the whole Walmart Butler group is hidden, so you only see the Amazon one. Upgrade any time in Settings, under Subscription.

paragraphs.heading: Same Deals panel, Walmart only
paragraphs.text: This is the same Deals Butler panel you already know, locked to Walmart. If you renamed your Deals Butler, that name shows up here too. The Overview shows posts today, posts queued, and the last and next search. A second Deals Butler gets its own Walmart Deals entry.

paragraphs.heading: Keywords
paragraphs.text: The Keywords tab is where you say what to look for. Add the kinds of products your followers buy, then set how big a discount counts as a deal.

paragraphs.heading: Search Deals
paragraphs.text: Search Deals is the engine. It searches Walmart for deals that match your keywords and filters. The results land in the table below, ready to post.

paragraphs.heading: Search now, or on a schedule
paragraphs.text: This button runs a search right now. Most people turn on the automatic search instead, so new deals show up on their own.

paragraphs.heading: Event Deals
paragraphs.text: Event Deals is Walmart only. During a big sale, Walmart publishes its featured deals. Pick the ones you want and add them to your queue. Nothing to search for.

paragraphs.heading: Search Deal Pages
paragraphs.text: Search Deal Pages searches Walmart's own deal pages. Save what it finds as drafts to review, or queue them to post on the next round.

paragraphs.heading: Build Your Post
paragraphs.text: Build Your Post sets the words. Your caption template fills in the product name, price and discount for every deal.

paragraphs.heading: Your Walmart posts
paragraphs.text: The Deals tab is the result. Every Walmart deal that is queued, scheduled or posted lives here, with its link.

paragraphs.heading: Where posting is set up
paragraphs.text: Where your posts go, and when, is set on the Deals Butler hub. Social Destinations, the Scheduler, and Take turns, which alternates Amazon and Walmart posts, all live there.

paragraphs.heading: Set your link provider first
paragraphs.text: One thing to set up first. Walmart Butler Settings picks who builds your links, Walmart Creator or Mavely. Until you pick one, Walmart deals stay paused, so your links always pay you.

paragraphs.heading: Next step
paragraphs.text: Your next step: open Walmart Butler Settings, pick a provider, then come back and add a few keywords.

vK0i1Zj0AKc.title: YouTube Butler: Upload Your Amazon Storefront Videos to YouTube With Affiliate Links

paragraphs.heading: Videos you already have
paragraphs.text: You have hundreds of shoppable videos on your storefront and a YouTube channel with none of them. YouTube Butler uploads them, titled, described, linked and thumbnailed, a batch a day, until the whole catalog is live.

paragraphs.heading: Power User feature
paragraphs.text: Quick note on plans. YouTube Butler is a Power User feature. On the Beginner plan it is hidden from the sidebar. Upgrade any time in Settings, under Subscription.

paragraphs.heading: What it needs
paragraphs.text: Storefront Butler synced at least once, and YouTube signed in in the browser the butler opens. Guided Setup walks every option in order if you would rather answer questions.

paragraphs.heading: Upload dashboard
paragraphs.text: The dashboard: total videos in inventory, queued, uploaded, how many are Shorts, regular videos, and failed.

paragraphs.heading: Import Past Harvests
paragraphs.text: Video Inventory fills itself when Storefront Butler harvests. Import Past Harvests pulls in what it already found.

paragraphs.heading: Find the right ones
paragraphs.text: Filter by orientation, status and duration, or search by title or ASIN. Vertical or square under three minutes becomes a Short; landscape stays a regular video.

paragraphs.heading: Queue them
paragraphs.text: Select the videos and Queue Selected lines them up. Do not upload keeps a video out for good; Allow again brings it back. Upload Now sends the selection straight away.

paragraphs.heading: Settings
paragraphs.text: Settings is where the upload is shaped. Visibility ships set to Public, so decide that first. Title and description come from AI or a template with the product filled in.

paragraphs.heading: Visibility
paragraphs.text: Visibility: Public, Unlisted or Private for every upload.

paragraphs.heading: Titles, links, AI
paragraphs.text: The title template, affiliate-tagged links in the description or pinned comment, Shorts hashtags, AI SEO titles with a spend cap, and AI thumbnails with their own cap. Max per session paces each run.

paragraphs.heading: Scheduler
paragraphs.text: The Scheduler uploads a batch a day: how often, how many per run, a start time, and the windows it may run in. Even a four thousand video storefront uploads itself over time.

paragraphs.heading: Upload Queued
paragraphs.text: Upload Queued drives YouTube Studio in a real browser on your signed-in Google profile and uploads everything in the queue. Watch it run in the top bar keeps it on screen. Accept Creator Connections also opts into campaigns for tagged products. Not pressed today.

paragraphs.heading: Upload Log
paragraphs.text: The Upload Log records every upload with its YouTube link and status, and Export CSV keeps the list.

paragraphs.heading: Next step
paragraphs.text: Your next step: run Guided Setup, set visibility to Unlisted for the first batch, queue five videos, and press Upload Queued while you watch.

x4Xkd-L1JmU.title: Getting Started With Influencer Butler: Your First Five Minutes

paragraphs.heading: Your first five minutes
paragraphs.text: You just installed Influencer Butler and signed in. Here is the five minute version: where things are, and how to run your first butler.

paragraphs.heading: The top bar
paragraphs.text: The top bar is always there. Your hourly rate, the hours and money the butlers have saved you, your storefront id, and whether automations are paused.

paragraphs.heading: Butlers live in the sidebar
paragraphs.text: Every butler lives in the sidebar, grouped by platform: Amazon, Walmart, Deals, Facebook, Instagram and more. Click a group name to open it.

paragraphs.heading: The Dashboard is home
paragraphs.text: The Dashboard is home. It shows what is running, what is scheduled today, and your numbers, all in one place.

paragraphs.heading: Your butlers at a glance
paragraphs.text: Lower down, one card per butler with its last run. Click a card to open that butler.

paragraphs.heading: A good first butler: Orders Butler
paragraphs.text: A good first butler is Orders Butler. It is free, and it only reads. It pulls your Amazon orders into the app so your earnings start showing up.

paragraphs.heading: Watch it run
paragraphs.text: See this eye at the top? That is Watch it run. On, you see the browser doing the work. Off, it runs in the background. Leave it on the first time.

paragraphs.heading: Press Run
paragraphs.text: Then press Run. The butler opens Chrome, signs in if it needs to, and reads your orders. You can watch, or go make coffee.

paragraphs.heading: If a site asks you to sign in

paragraphs.heading: Help and Tutorials
paragraphs.text: Stuck? Help and Tutorials has a written guide for every butler, and a video for most. The Watch the tutorial button on each panel opens the same video.

paragraphs.heading: Ask the AI assistant
paragraphs.text: Or ask the AI assistant in plain words. It knows every butler and can walk you to the right screen.

paragraphs.heading: Next step
paragraphs.text: Your next step: open Orders Butler and press Run. Then come back to the Dashboard and watch your numbers appear.

y47-S58jX1Y.title: Daily Commission Butler: Accept Creator Connections Campaigns From Your Sales

paragraphs.heading: Campaigns on what you already sell
paragraphs.text: Brands run Creator Connections campaigns that pay extra on products you are already selling. Finding them one by one every day is the job nobody does. Daily Commission Butler does it for you.

paragraphs.heading: Included in the Beginner plan
paragraphs.text: Quick note on plans. Daily Commission Butler is included in the Beginner plan, so everyone has it.

paragraphs.heading: What it does
paragraphs.text: It reads your recent sales, looks for a campaign on each of those exact products, and accepts the ones it finds. It also checks your storefront's best sellers, so a top product with an open campaign is never left unclaimed.

paragraphs.heading: Accepting is a promise
paragraphs.text: Accepting a campaign is a promise to a brand, and it cannot be undone from here. So in this video I show every setting and press nothing.

paragraphs.heading: Before you run it
paragraphs.text: Two things first. Run CC Check at least once so the campaign catalog is fresh, and have Orders Butler synced in the last couple of days. Those supply the sales it matches against.

paragraphs.heading: Marketplaces
paragraphs.text: Marketplaces: tick every Amazon country where you earn. One run sweeps them all, and the storefront URL beside each one is optional.

paragraphs.heading: Your earnings
paragraphs.text: The earnings cards: lifetime earnings from accepted campaigns, the rolling thirty days, and the total accepted. Show in lets you pick the currency.

paragraphs.heading: Day range
paragraphs.text: Day range chooses how far back it looks at your sales. Today is the smallest, safest start. Seven days catches products that sold slowly, and thirty days goes wider still.

paragraphs.heading: Watch it run
paragraphs.text: Watch it run in the top bar opens the browser so you can see it work. Handy the first time. It applies to every butler.

paragraphs.heading: Run
paragraphs.text: Run starts it. It signs into Amazon, reads the sales for the range you ticked, and accepts every campaign that matches a product code exactly. Read the status badge while it works.

paragraphs.heading: On a schedule
paragraphs.text: Once you trust it, put it on a schedule. A start time and a repeat interval, then Enable Schedule, and it says yes to brands while you get on with your day.

paragraphs.heading: Enable Schedule
paragraphs.text: Enable Schedule turns the timer on. Stop Schedule turns it off and clears anything waiting.

paragraphs.heading: What it accepted
paragraphs.text: The log is the record: every campaign it accepted, the commission, the deal details, and whether that product has a video carousel yet. Filter it, send products to Content Butler, or export it.

paragraphs.heading: All Time
paragraphs.text: All Time swaps between the recent view and your whole history.

paragraphs.heading: Next step
paragraphs.text: Your next step: run CC Check, tick Today, press Run once yourself, and read what it accepted. Then set the schedule to once a day.

yMKugbCmY8s.title: Amazon Butler Hub Tour: Every Amazon Butler On One Screen

paragraphs.heading: One screen for every Amazon butler
paragraphs.text: Amazon Butler is the biggest group in the app, more than twenty butlers. This hub keeps them all on one screen.

paragraphs.heading: Both plans, different cards
paragraphs.text: A note on plans. The hub shows on both plans. On the Beginner plan you see the Beginner butlers' cards, like Message Brands, Orders and Daily Commission. The Power User cards, like Goldmine and Earnings Intelligence, appear once you upgrade.

paragraphs.heading: Sign-in and settings
paragraphs.text: Up top, whether Amazon is signed in, and a shortcut to your Creators API key, which lives in Amazon Butler Settings.

paragraphs.heading: Creator Stars
paragraphs.text: The Creator Stars card. Your current tier, your points this quarter, days left, and whether you are on pace for Gold or Platinum. It fills in from your storefront on each Amazon check.

paragraphs.heading: Today
paragraphs.text: Today's numbers for the group: brands contacted, what is active now, what is scheduled.

paragraphs.heading: Your Amazon performance
paragraphs.text: Your Amazon performance over 30 days, against the 30 days before. Earnings, revenue, clicks, orders. Tick Email me this every day to get it in your inbox.

paragraphs.heading: Activity digest email
paragraphs.text: The activity digest is a running check-in by email: deals sent, deals held and why, and anything waiting for a sign-in. Hourly, daily or weekly.

paragraphs.heading: Butlers in this group
paragraphs.text: And the cards. One per butler, with its last run, Open, Run, and Watch the tutorial, which plays that butler's video right here.

paragraphs.heading: Next step
paragraphs.text: Your next step: press Watch the tutorial on the card you are curious about.

YoJadCTQFFg.title: Photo Reload Butler: Re-Post Your Amazon Photos to Other Marketplaces

paragraphs.heading: Same idea, for photos
paragraphs.text: This is the photo version of Video Reload. It takes the shoppable photos already on your storefront and re-posts them to the other marketplaces, so one image earns in every store you are eligible for.

paragraphs.heading: Included in the Beginner plan
paragraphs.text: Quick note on plans. Photo Reload Butler is included in the Beginner plan, so everyone has it.

paragraphs.heading: It reads Storefront Butler
paragraphs.text: It reads your photos from the Storefront Butler table, so sync that first. It posts to your real storefronts, so nothing is pressed today.

paragraphs.heading: Step 1: preferred formulas
paragraphs.text: Three steps. Step one opens with Preferred Formulas: fan out US photos to Canada, the UK, Australia and Singapore, a US re-upload, reload my proven winners, or in-stock products only. One press fills in the source, destinations and filters.

paragraphs.heading: Source and destinations
paragraphs.text: Or set them yourself. Photo source is the marketplace your photos live on, and Upload destinations are where the copies go, each with its own sign-in.

paragraphs.heading: Skip unavailable products
paragraphs.text: Skip products that are currently unavailable checks stock first, so you are not posting dead links.

paragraphs.heading: Step 2: what to process
paragraphs.text: Step two: a timeframe, and Max photos per run. Ten is plenty the first time.

paragraphs.heading: Skip duplicates
paragraphs.text: Skip duplicates stops the same image posting twice: same title, same product, or already posted to that marketplace.

paragraphs.heading: Step 3: run mode
paragraphs.text: Step three is the one to read twice. Run mode: Post and keep the original is the safe choice. The other modes remove the original from Amazon, after saving a copy to your computer.

paragraphs.heading: Winners and fresh titles
paragraphs.text: Winners first reloads only photos whose products earned commissions. Refresh the title gives each copy a new hook, and Translate titles writes them in each marketplace's language.

paragraphs.heading: Run
paragraphs.text: Run opens Chrome, reads each eligible photo, and posts it to the destinations you picked. Watch it run in the top bar keeps the browser on screen.

paragraphs.heading: The photo log
paragraphs.text: The Photo Log tab records every post with its destinations and status. Deleted from Amazon keeps the originals it removed, and Reload Deleted Photos can post them back.

paragraphs.heading: Next step
paragraphs.text: Your next step: press Fan out US photos, set max photos to ten, keep Post and keep the original, and run it once.

zjQUvhYF5Os.title: Benable Like Butler: Auto-Like Collections, Free

paragraphs.heading: Hearts by hand take forever
paragraphs.text: Tapping hearts on Benable collections by hand takes forever. Like Butler does it for you, and it is free.

paragraphs.heading: Switch it on first
paragraphs.text: If it is missing under Benable Butler, open Show / Hide Butlers and turn it on. It can start hidden.

paragraphs.heading: Sign in to Benable first
paragraphs.text: Sign in to Benable here first. Watch it run, at the top, shows or hides the browser. Off and signed out, the run stops.

paragraphs.heading: Who to visit
paragraphs.text: Add Benable profile links here, one per row. Each row's Max likes box is optional. Empty means it uses the main limit.

paragraphs.heading: Optional: Discover
paragraphs.text: Discover is optional. It also likes collections, and the items inside them, from Benable's Discover page, after your profiles. You can run with Discover alone.

paragraphs.heading: Pick Discover categories
paragraphs.text: Pick from 14 categories, like Fashion and Tech. Trending is ticked at first. Only ticked ones are visited.

paragraphs.heading: What gets a heart
paragraphs.text: Then what gets a heart: collections, items inside them, or both. With both on, collections come first.

paragraphs.heading: Cap items per collection
paragraphs.text: Max items per collection stops one huge collection using up the run. It starts at 50.

paragraphs.heading: One total for the run
paragraphs.text: Max likes per run is one total for the whole run, across all profiles and Discover. It starts at 10.

paragraphs.heading: Wait between hearts
paragraphs.text: Delay between likes starts at 8 seconds, plus a small random extra. It accepts 2 to 90.

paragraphs.heading: Three speed presets
paragraphs.text: Presets: Fast is 3 seconds, Normal is 8, Careful is 15. For a first run, pick Careful.

paragraphs.heading: Check all is ticked
paragraphs.text: Check all is ticked at first. It ignores the butler's own record of past runs. Untick it, and it also skips anything it already logged.

paragraphs.heading: These are real likes
paragraphs.text: Start begins the run in the browser. There is no dry run, so every heart is a real like, and this app cannot take one back.

paragraphs.heading: Pause and Stop
paragraphs.text: Pause holds a run. Stop appears only during a run, and ends it and closes the browser.

paragraphs.heading: Pick a start time
paragraphs.text: Scheduler: pick a start time. The first run happens then, and a time in the past moves forward to about a minute from now.

paragraphs.heading: How often to repeat
paragraphs.text: Repeat every is in minutes, from 15 to 720. Pick how often the run should repeat.

paragraphs.heading: Turn the schedule on
paragraphs.text: Enable Schedule turns it on. While it is on, the profiles, Discover and limits lock, along with Start, Stop and Pause. Stop Schedule unlocks them.

paragraphs.heading: What it has liked
paragraphs.text: History lists each creator you liked, with counts and latest activity. Search it, or filter by 24 hours, 7 days or 30 days.

paragraphs.heading: Clearing the log
paragraphs.text: Clear all empties the log, after asking. Undo last clear brings it back. Total likes is counted from that log, so Reset total clears it too.

paragraphs.heading: Where the list goes next
paragraphs.text: Your profile list can be copied into Comment Butler, a Pro butler, with its Import button.

paragraphs.heading: Your first run
paragraphs.text: First run: one profile, Max likes 10, Careful, Watch it run on. Then press Start yourself.
